en_def: to exist, or to have a quality, job, or position (am / is / are / was / were)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often drop 'am/is/are' or replace them with 'myself' ('Myself Balvant'). English always needs the verb 'be' before a noun or adjective.

examples.en: I am a security engineer.
examples.hi: मैं एक सिक्योरिटी इंजीनियर हूँ।

examples.en: She is tired today.
examples.hi: वह आज थकी हुई है।

examples.en: They are at the office.
examples.hi: वे ऑफ़िस में हैं।

examples.en: It was cold last night.
examples.hi: कल रात ठंड थी।

examples.en: We were late for the meeting.
examples.hi: हम मीटिंग के लिए देर से पहुँचे थे।

examples.en: Is he your brother?
examples.hi: क्या वह आपका भाई है?

common_mistake.wrong: Myself Balvant, I am working in Ahmedabad.
common_mistake.right: I am Balvant, and I work in Ahmedabad.
common_mistake.why: 'Myself' is never used to introduce yourself; use 'I am' + name.

cloze.sentence: My parents ____ from Gujarat.

en_def: to own or hold something; to experience something
hi_nuance: Do not say 'I am having a car'. For possession, 'have' is never continuous. 'Having' is only for eating or experiencing ('I am having lunch').

examples.en: I have two brothers.
examples.hi: मेरे दो भाई हैं।

examples.en: Do you have a minute?
examples.hi: क्या आपके पास एक मिनट है?

examples.en: She has a new phone.
examples.hi: उसके पास नया फ़ोन है।

examples.en: We had a good time in Goa.
examples.hi: गोवा में हमने अच्छा समय बिताया।

examples.en: He doesn't have any money.
examples.hi: उसके पास कोई पैसा नहीं है।

examples.en: Let's have lunch together.
examples.hi: चलो साथ में लंच करते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I am having two laptops.
common_mistake.right: I have two laptops.
common_mistake.why: Possession uses simple 'have', not the continuous form.

cloze.sentence: We ____ a meeting at ten o'clock.

en_def: to perform an action or task; also a helper verb for questions and negatives
hi_def: करना; प्रश्न और नकारात्मक वाक्य बनाने में सहायक क्रिया
hi_nuance: Hindi 'करना' covers both 'do' and 'make'. Use 'do' for work, tasks, and activities; use 'make' for creating things ('make a decision', not 'do a decision').

examples.en: What do you do on Sundays?
examples.hi: आप रविवार को क्या करते हैं?

examples.en: I do my homework in the evening.
examples.hi: मैं शाम को अपना होमवर्क करता हूँ।

examples.en: She does yoga every morning.
examples.hi: वह हर सुबह योग करती है।

examples.en: Did you do the report?
examples.hi: क्या आपने रिपोर्ट बना ली?

examples.en: We don't do that here.
examples.hi: हम यहाँ ऐसा नहीं करते।

common_mistake.wrong: Please do the needful.
common_mistake.right: Please take care of this.
common_mistake.why: 'Do the needful' is an Indianism; native speakers say what exactly should be done.

cloze.sentence: What ____ you do for a living?

en_def: to speak words; to express something in words
hi_nuance: 'Say' takes no person as object: 'He said to me', not 'He said me'. Use 'tell' when you name the listener: 'He told me'.

examples.en: What did you say?
examples.hi: आपने क्या कहा?

examples.en: She said she was busy.
examples.hi: उसने कहा कि वह व्यस्त है।

examples.en: Say hello to your mother.
examples.hi: अपनी माँ को नमस्ते कहना।

examples.en: He always says the same thing.
examples.hi: वह हमेशा एक ही बात कहता है।

examples.en: I said sorry, but he didn't listen.
examples.hi: मैंने माफ़ी माँगी, लेकिन उसने नहीं सुना।

common_mistake.wrong: He said me to wait.
common_mistake.right: He told me to wait.
common_mistake.why: 'Say' cannot take a person directly as its object; 'tell' can.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ that again slowly.

en_def: to move from one place to another; to leave
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers say 'I am going to office' — English needs 'the': 'going to the office'. Also 'I have gone yesterday' is wrong; use 'I went yesterday'.

examples.en: I go to work by bus.
examples.hi: मैं बस से काम पर जाता हूँ।

examples.en: Where are you going?
examples.hi: आप कहाँ जा रहे हैं?

examples.en: She went home early.
examples.hi: वह जल्दी घर चली गई।

examples.en: Let's go for a walk.
examples.hi: चलो टहलने चलते हैं।

examples.en: The train goes every ten minutes.
examples.hi: ट्रेन हर दस मिनट में जाती है।

examples.en: He has gone to Mumbai.
examples.hi: वह मुंबई गया हुआ है।

common_mistake.wrong: I have gone to Delhi yesterday.
common_mistake.right: I went to Delhi yesterday.
common_mistake.why: A finished time word like 'yesterday' needs the past simple, not present perfect.

cloze.sentence: We ____ to the market every Saturday.

en_def: to receive, obtain, or become
hi_nuance: Hindi 'मिलना' is often translated as 'meet', but for receiving things it is 'get': 'I got a job', not 'I met a job'. 'Get' + adjective means 'become': 'get tired'.

examples.en: I got a new job last month.
examples.hi: मुझे पिछले महीने नई नौकरी मिली।

examples.en: Did you get my email?
examples.hi: क्या आपको मेरा ईमेल मिला?

examples.en: It gets cold in December.
examples.hi: दिसंबर में ठंड हो जाती है।

examples.en: Can you get some milk on the way?
examples.hi: क्या आप रास्ते में थोड़ा दूध ले सकते हैं?

examples.en: She gets up at six.
examples.hi: वह छह बजे उठती है।

common_mistake.wrong: I am not getting what you say.
common_mistake.right: I don't understand what you're saying.
common_mistake.why: 'Getting' for 'understand' is fine only in very casual speech; in normal speech use 'understand'.

cloze.sentence: I usually ____ home at seven.

en_def: to create or produce something; to cause something to happen
hi_nuance: Many Hindi 'करना' phrases need 'make' in English: make a decision, make a mistake, make a call, make friends. Not 'do a mistake'.

examples.en: My mother makes great tea.
examples.hi: मेरी माँ बहुत अच्छी चाय बनाती हैं।

examples.en: Don't make a noise.
examples.hi: शोर मत करो।

examples.en: We need to make a decision today.
examples.hi: हमें आज एक फ़ैसला लेना है।

examples.en: He made a mistake in the report.
examples.hi: उसने रिपोर्ट में एक गलती की।

examples.en: She makes friends easily.
examples.hi: वह आसानी से दोस्त बना लेती है।

common_mistake.wrong: I did a mistake.
common_mistake.right: I made a mistake.
common_mistake.why: 'Mistake' collocates with 'make', not 'do'.

cloze.sentence: Can you ____ me a cup of coffee?

en_def: to have information or understanding in your mind; to be familiar with someone
hi_nuance: 'Know' is a state verb — never 'I am knowing'. Also, 'I know him' means you have met him; for facts say 'I know that…'.

examples.en: I know the answer.
examples.hi: मुझे जवाब पता है।

examples.en: Do you know her name?
examples.hi: क्या आप उसका नाम जानते हैं?

examples.en: He knows a lot about computers.
examples.hi: वह कंप्यूटर के बारे में बहुत जानता है।

examples.en: I didn't know you were here.
examples.hi: मुझे नहीं पता था कि आप यहाँ हैं।

examples.en: We have known each other for years.
examples.hi: हम एक-दूसरे को सालों से जानते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I am knowing this person very well.
common_mistake.right: I know this person very well.
common_mistake.why: 'Know' is a state verb and does not take the continuous form.

cloze.sentence: Do you ____ where the station is?

en_def: to carry or move something with you; to accept; to need an amount of time
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers say 'take a decision'; English prefers 'make a decision'. But 'take a photo', 'take a break', 'take medicine' are correct.

examples.en: Take your umbrella; it might rain.
examples.hi: अपना छाता ले लो; बारिश हो सकती है।

examples.en: It takes an hour to get there.
examples.hi: वहाँ पहुँचने में एक घंटा लगता है।

examples.en: She took a photo of the sunset.
examples.hi: उसने सूर्यास्त की फ़ोटो ली।

examples.en: Take the medicine after food.
examples.hi: खाने के बाद दवा लो।

examples.en: Let's take a break.
examples.hi: चलो थोड़ा ब्रेक लेते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: We will take a decision tomorrow.
common_mistake.right: We will make a decision tomorrow.
common_mistake.why: 'Decision' collocates with 'make' in natural English.

cloze.sentence: How long does it ____ to reach the airport?

en_def: to notice something with your eyes; to understand; to meet someone
hi_nuance: 'See' is not used in the continuous for the sense of sight: 'I see a bird', not 'I am seeing a bird'. 'I'm seeing someone' means dating.

examples.en: I can see the mountains from here.
examples.hi: मैं यहाँ से पहाड़ देख सकता हूँ।

examples.en: See you tomorrow!
examples.hi: कल मिलते हैं!

examples.en: Did you see the match last night?
examples.hi: क्या आपने कल रात मैच देखा?

examples.en: I see what you mean.
examples.hi: मैं समझ गया आप क्या कहना चाहते हैं।

examples.en: She saw a doctor about her back.
examples.hi: उसने अपनी पीठ के लिए डॉक्टर को दिखाया।

common_mistake.wrong: I am seeing a problem in the code.
common_mistake.right: I can see a problem in the code.
common_mistake.why: For the sense of sight, use 'can see' or simple 'see', not continuous.

cloze.sentence: Can you ____ the board from there?

en_def: to move toward the speaker or to a place
hi_nuance: Hindi 'आना' is also used for 'know how to' ('मुझे तैरना आता है'). In English use 'can': 'I can swim', never 'swimming comes to me'.

examples.en: Come here, please.
examples.hi: कृपया यहाँ आइए।

examples.en: My friend is coming to dinner.
examples.hi: मेरा दोस्त डिनर पर आ रहा है।

examples.en: Where do you come from?
examples.hi: आप कहाँ से हैं?

examples.en: The bus came late.
examples.hi: बस देर से आई।

examples.en: Summer is coming.
examples.hi: गर्मी आ रही है।

common_mistake.wrong: English does not come to me.
common_mistake.right: I can't speak English well.
common_mistake.why: The Hindi structure 'आना' for skills does not translate; use 'can'.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ to my office at three.

en_def: to have an opinion; to use your mind
hi_nuance: The 'th' is a soft, airy sound with the tongue between the teeth, not the Hindi 'थ'. 'I think' (opinion) is simple; 'I am thinking about it' (process) is continuous.

examples.en: I think it will rain.
examples.hi: मुझे लगता है कि बारिश होगी।

examples.en: What do you think of the plan?
examples.hi: आप इस योजना के बारे में क्या सोचते हैं?

examples.en: Let me think for a moment.
examples.hi: मुझे एक पल सोचने दो।

examples.en: She is thinking about changing jobs.
examples.hi: वह नौकरी बदलने के बारे में सोच रही है।

examples.en: I thought you were at home.
examples.hi: मुझे लगा कि आप घर पर हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I am thinking it is correct.
common_mistake.right: I think it is correct.
common_mistake.why: For opinions, use simple 'think', not continuous.

cloze.sentence: I ____ he is right.

en_def: to turn your eyes toward something; to seem
hi_nuance: 'Look at' needs 'at': 'look at the screen'. Without 'at', 'look' means 'seem': 'You look tired'.

examples.en: Look at this photo.
examples.hi: इस फ़ोटो को देखो।

examples.en: You look happy today.
examples.hi: आप आज खुश दिख रहे हैं।

examples.en: I'm looking for my keys.
examples.hi: मैं अपनी चाबियाँ ढूँढ रहा हूँ।

examples.en: He looked out of the window.
examples.hi: उसने खिड़की से बाहर देखा।

examples.en: It looks like rain.
examples.hi: लगता है बारिश होने वाली है।

common_mistake.wrong: Look the board carefully.
common_mistake.right: Look at the board carefully.
common_mistake.why: 'Look' needs the preposition 'at' before an object.

cloze.sentence: ____ at the map before you drive.

en_def: to wish for or desire something
hi_nuance: 'Want' is a state verb: 'I want tea', never 'I am wanting tea'. It takes 'to' + verb: 'I want to go', not 'I want go'.

examples.en: I want a cup of tea.
examples.hi: मुझे एक कप चाय चाहिए।

examples.en: Do you want to come with us?
examples.hi: क्या आप हमारे साथ आना चाहते हैं?

examples.en: She wants a new laptop.
examples.hi: वह नया लैपटॉप चाहती है।

examples.en: They wanted to leave early.
examples.hi: वे जल्दी निकलना चाहते थे।

examples.en: What do you want for dinner?
examples.hi: आप रात के खाने में क्या चाहते हैं?

common_mistake.wrong: I am wanting to learn English.
common_mistake.right: I want to learn English.
common_mistake.why: 'Want' is a state verb and is not used in the continuous.

cloze.sentence: Do you ____ some water?

en_def: to hand something to someone; to provide
hi_nuance: Hindi 'देना' phrases differ: 'give an exam' is wrong — students 'take' or 'sit' an exam; teachers 'give' exams. 'Give a call' is fine in speech.

examples.en: Give me the keys, please.
examples.hi: मुझे चाबियाँ दो, कृपया।

examples.en: She gave him a present.
examples.hi: उसने उसे एक तोहफ़ा दिया।

examples.en: I'll give you a call tonight.
examples.hi: मैं आज रात आपको फ़ोन करूँगा।

examples.en: They gave us good news.
examples.hi: उन्होंने हमें अच्छी ख़बर दी।

examples.en: Can you give me some advice?
examples.hi: क्या आप मुझे कुछ सलाह दे सकते हैं?

common_mistake.wrong: I am giving my exam tomorrow.
common_mistake.right: I am taking my exam tomorrow.
common_mistake.why: Students take exams; teachers give them.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ this file to the manager.

en_def: to do something with a tool or thing for a purpose
hi_nuance: The verb ends in a /z/ sound; the noun 'use' ends in /s/. 'Used to' (past habit) is a different structure: 'I used to smoke'.

examples.en: Can I use your phone?
examples.hi: क्या मैं आपका फ़ोन इस्तेमाल कर सकता हूँ?

examples.en: We use a password manager at work.
examples.hi: हम काम पर पासवर्ड मैनेजर का उपयोग करते हैं।

examples.en: She uses too much salt.
examples.hi: वह बहुत ज़्यादा नमक इस्तेमाल करती है।

examples.en: I used the stairs because the lift was broken.
examples.hi: लिफ़्ट खराब थी इसलिए मैंने सीढ़ियाँ इस्तेमाल कीं।

examples.en: Don't use this word in an email.
examples.hi: ईमेल में इस शब्द का इस्तेमाल मत करो।

common_mistake.wrong: I am not use to this weather.
common_mistake.right: I am not used to this weather.
common_mistake.why: 'Be used to' needs the -d ending; it means 'accustomed to'.

cloze.sentence: Can I ____ your charger for a minute?

en_def: to discover something you were looking for, or by chance
hi_nuance: 'Find' is the result; 'look for' or 'search' is the action. 'I am finding my keys' is wrong — say 'I am looking for my keys'.

examples.en: I can't find my glasses.
examples.hi: मुझे मेरा चश्मा नहीं मिल रहा।

examples.en: Did you find the bug?
examples.hi: क्या आपको बग मिला?

examples.en: She found a wallet on the road.
examples.hi: उसे सड़क पर एक बटुआ मिला।

examples.en: We found a good restaurant nearby.
examples.hi: हमें पास में एक अच्छा रेस्तराँ मिला।

examples.en: I find this book very interesting.
examples.hi: मुझे यह किताब बहुत दिलचस्प लगती है।

common_mistake.wrong: I am finding my phone since morning.
common_mistake.right: I have been looking for my phone since morning.
common_mistake.why: 'Find' is the result, not the search; use 'look for'.

cloze.sentence: Did you ____ the file I sent?

en_def: to give information to a person in words
hi_nuance: 'Tell' always names the listener: 'tell me', 'tell him'. 'Tell to me' is wrong. Compare 'say' (no listener named).

examples.en: Tell me your name.
examples.hi: मुझे अपना नाम बताओ।

examples.en: She told me the truth.
examples.hi: उसने मुझे सच बताया।

examples.en: Can you tell him I called?
examples.hi: क्या आप उसे बता सकते हैं कि मैंने फ़ोन किया था?

examples.en: He tells great stories.
examples.hi: वह बहुत अच्छी कहानियाँ सुनाता है।

examples.en: I told you it would work.
examples.hi: मैंने आपसे कहा था कि यह काम करेगा।

common_mistake.wrong: He told to me about the meeting.
common_mistake.right: He told me about the meeting.
common_mistake.why: 'Tell' takes the person directly, without 'to'.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ me when you arrive.

en_def: to say something in order to get an answer or information; to request
hi_nuance: Pronounce the final cluster /sk/ clearly: 'asked' is /ɑːskt/, not 'aksed' or 'ask-ed'. Also 'ask a question' — never 'ask a doubt'.

examples.en: Can I ask you a question?
examples.hi: क्या मैं आपसे एक सवाल पूछ सकता हूँ?

examples.en: She asked me for help.
examples.hi: उसने मुझसे मदद माँगी।

examples.en: Ask him where the meeting is.
examples.hi: उससे पूछो कि मीटिंग कहाँ है।

examples.en: They asked for the bill.
examples.hi: उन्होंने बिल माँगा।

examples.en: I asked about the price.
examples.hi: मैंने कीमत के बारे में पूछा।

common_mistake.wrong: I have a doubt, can I ask?
common_mistake.right: I have a question, can I ask?
common_mistake.why: 'Doubt' means you don't believe something; for an unclear point use 'question'.

cloze.sentence: If you don't understand, ____ the teacher.

en_def: to do a job; (of a machine) to function
hi_nuance: 'Work' as a noun is uncountable: 'a lot of work', never 'works' or 'a work'. 'I am working in TCS' → native speakers say 'I work at TCS' for a permanent job.

examples.en: I work from nine to six.
examples.hi: मैं नौ से छह बजे तक काम करता हूँ।

examples.en: My laptop doesn't work.
examples.hi: मेरा लैपटॉप काम नहीं कर रहा।

examples.en: She works at a bank.
examples.hi: वह एक बैंक में काम करती है।

examples.en: The plan worked well.
examples.hi: योजना अच्छी तरह काम कर गई।

examples.en: We worked late last night.
examples.hi: हमने कल रात देर तक काम किया।

common_mistake.wrong: I am working in Infosys since 2019.
common_mistake.right: I have worked at Infosys since 2019.
common_mistake.why: 'Since' + start point needs the present perfect, and companies take 'at'.

cloze.sentence: Does the printer ____ now?

en_def: to appear to be a certain way
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers under-use 'seem' and over-use 'is'. 'He seems tired' is softer and more natural than 'He is tired' when you are guessing.

examples.en: You seem tired.
examples.hi: आप थके हुए लगते हैं।

examples.en: It seems like a good idea.
examples.hi: यह एक अच्छा विचार लगता है।

examples.en: She seemed happy with the result.
examples.hi: वह नतीजे से खुश लग रही थी।

examples.en: The shop seems to be closed.
examples.hi: दुकान बंद लगती है।

examples.en: It seems that nobody knows.
examples.hi: लगता है किसी को पता नहीं है।

common_mistake.wrong: It is seeming difficult.
common_mistake.right: It seems difficult.
common_mistake.why: 'Seem' is a state verb and is not used in the continuous.

cloze.sentence: He ____ to know everyone here.

en_def: to experience an emotion or physical sensation; to touch
hi_nuance: 'I am feeling' and 'I feel' are both fine for emotions. But 'I feel like' + -ing means 'want to': 'I feel like eating pizza'.

examples.en: I feel much better today.
examples.hi: मैं आज बहुत बेहतर महसूस कर रहा हूँ।

examples.en: How do you feel about the new job?
examples.hi: नई नौकरी के बारे में आप कैसा महसूस करते हैं?

examples.en: She felt cold, so she closed the window.
examples.hi: उसे ठंड लगी, इसलिए उसने खिड़की बंद कर दी।

examples.en: I feel like having a coffee.
examples.hi: मेरा कॉफ़ी पीने का मन है।

examples.en: Feel this cloth — it's very soft.
examples.hi: इस कपड़े को छूकर देखो — यह बहुत मुलायम है।

common_mistake.wrong: I am feeling to sleep.
common_mistake.right: I feel like sleeping.
common_mistake.why: 'Feel like' + -ing expresses wanting to do something.

cloze.sentence: Do you ____ okay? You look pale.

en_def: to attempt to do something; to test something
hi_nuance: 'Try to do' = attempt; 'try doing' = experiment. Hindi speakers often say 'try to' where 'try' + -ing is more natural: 'Try restarting the router'.

examples.en: I'll try to call you later.
examples.hi: मैं बाद में आपको फ़ोन करने की कोशिश करूँगा।

examples.en: Try this cake; it's delicious.
examples.hi: यह केक चखो; बहुत स्वादिष्ट है।

examples.en: She tried her best.
examples.hi: उसने पूरी कोशिश की।

examples.en: Have you tried restarting the computer?
examples.hi: क्या आपने कंप्यूटर रीस्टार्ट करके देखा?

examples.en: Let me try again.
examples.hi: मुझे फिर से कोशिश करने दो।

common_mistake.wrong: I tried for calling him.
common_mistake.right: I tried to call him.
common_mistake.why: 'Try' is followed by 'to' + verb, not 'for' + -ing.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ to be on time.

en_def: to go away from a place; to let something stay where it is
hi_nuance: Indian English uses 'leave' as a noun for holiday ('I am on leave') — that is fine. But 'leave me' meaning 'let me go' sounds rude; say 'let me go'.

examples.en: I leave home at eight.
examples.hi: मैं आठ बजे घर से निकलता हूँ।

examples.en: She left her bag on the bus.
examples.hi: वह अपना बैग बस में छोड़ आई।

examples.en: Leave the door open.
examples.hi: दरवाज़ा खुला छोड़ दो।

examples.en: He is leaving the company next month.
examples.hi: वह अगले महीने कंपनी छोड़ रहा है।

examples.en: Please leave a message.
examples.hi: कृपया एक संदेश छोड़ दें।

common_mistake.wrong: I will leave from office at six.
common_mistake.right: I will leave the office at six.
common_mistake.why: 'Leave' takes the place directly, without 'from'.

cloze.sentence: What time does the train ____?

en_def: to phone someone; to give a name to; to shout
hi_nuance: 'Call me' means phone me. 'I will call you' is enough — 'I will call you up' is old-fashioned. 'Called as' is wrong: 'It is called a router', not 'called as a router'.

examples.en: Call me when you get home.
examples.hi: घर पहुँचकर मुझे फ़ोन करना।

examples.en: What is this called in English?
examples.hi: इसे अंग्रेज़ी में क्या कहते हैं?

examples.en: She called her son for dinner.
examples.hi: उसने अपने बेटे को खाने के लिए बुलाया।

examples.en: He called the office twice.
examples.hi: उसने ऑफ़िस में दो बार फ़ोन किया।

examples.en: They called their dog Bruno.
examples.hi: उन्होंने अपने कुत्ते का नाम ब्रूनो रखा।

common_mistake.wrong: This tool is called as Burp Suite.
common_mistake.right: This tool is called Burp Suite.
common_mistake.why: 'Called' is never followed by 'as'.

cloze.sentence: I'll ____ you back in five minutes.

en_def: to require something because it is necessary
hi_nuance: Hindi 'चाहिए' can mean both 'want' and 'need'. Use 'need' for necessity and 'want' for wishes. 'Need' is a state verb — no continuous.

examples.en: I need some help.
examples.hi: मुझे थोड़ी मदद चाहिए।

examples.en: Do you need anything from the shop?
examples.hi: क्या आपको दुकान से कुछ चाहिए?

examples.en: She needs to rest.
examples.hi: उसे आराम करने की ज़रूरत है।

examples.en: We need more time.
examples.hi: हमें और समय चाहिए।

examples.en: You don't need to come early.
examples.hi: आपको जल्दी आने की ज़रूरत नहीं है।

common_mistake.wrong: I am needing your signature.
common_mistake.right: I need your signature.
common_mistake.why: 'Need' is a state verb; use the simple form.

cloze.sentence: You ____ a visa to travel there.

en_def: to begin to be something; to change into
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often use 'become' where English uses 'get' + adjective in speech: 'get angry', 'get late'. 'Become' is slightly more formal.

examples.en: She became a doctor in 2020.
examples.hi: वह 2020 में डॉक्टर बनी।

examples.en: It became dark very quickly.
examples.hi: बहुत जल्दी अँधेरा हो गया।

examples.en: They became good friends.
examples.hi: वे अच्छे दोस्त बन गए।

examples.en: The city has become very expensive.
examples.hi: शहर बहुत महँगा हो गया है।

examples.en: I want to become a better speaker.
examples.hi: मैं एक बेहतर वक्ता बनना चाहता हूँ।

common_mistake.wrong: I became late for the bus.
common_mistake.right: I was late for the bus.
common_mistake.why: 'Become late' is unnatural; use 'be late' or 'get late' (informal).

cloze.sentence: He wants to ____ an engineer.

en_def: to place something somewhere
hi_nuance: The vowel is short /ʊ/ like 'book', not 'poot'. 'Put' always needs a place: 'Put it on the table', not just 'Put it'.

examples.en: Put the cup on the table.
examples.hi: कप को मेज़ पर रखो।

examples.en: Where did you put my keys?
examples.hi: तुमने मेरी चाबियाँ कहाँ रखीं?

examples.en: She put on her coat.
examples.hi: उसने अपना कोट पहना।

examples.en: Put some sugar in the tea.
examples.hi: चाय में थोड़ी चीनी डालो।

examples.en: He put the phone down.
examples.hi: उसने फ़ोन नीचे रख दिया।

common_mistake.wrong: Put the light.
common_mistake.right: Turn on the light.
common_mistake.why: Lights are 'turned' or 'switched' on/off, not 'put'.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ your bag under the seat.

en_def: to have a particular meaning; to intend
hi_nuance: 'What means this?' is Hindi word order. English: 'What does this mean?' 'I mean' is a common filler for clarifying — use it, but not every sentence.

examples.en: What does this word mean?
examples.hi: इस शब्द का क्या मतलब है?

examples.en: I didn't mean to hurt you.
examples.hi: मेरा आपको दुख पहुँचाने का इरादा नहीं था।

examples.en: A red light means stop.
examples.hi: लाल बत्ती का मतलब है रुको।

examples.en: She means well.
examples.hi: उसका इरादा अच्छा है।

examples.en: This means we have to start again.
examples.hi: इसका मतलब है कि हमें फिर से शुरू करना होगा।

common_mistake.wrong: What means 'remediation'?
common_mistake.right: What does 'remediation' mean?
common_mistake.why: Questions need 'does' + subject + base verb.

cloze.sentence: What do you ____ by 'later'?

en_def: to continue to have something; to continue doing something
hi_nuance: 'Keep' + -ing means continue: 'keep going', 'keep trying'. Hindi speakers sometimes say 'keep' where 'put' is meant: 'Keep it on the table' means leave it there permanently; for a moment, say 'put'.

examples.en: Keep the change.
examples.hi: बाकी पैसे रख लो।

examples.en: Keep trying; you'll get it.
examples.hi: कोशिश करते रहो; तुम कर लोगे।

examples.en: She keeps her desk very tidy.
examples.hi: वह अपनी मेज़ बहुत साफ़ रखती है।

examples.en: Keep this a secret.
examples.hi: इसे राज़ रखना।

examples.en: He kept talking during the film.
examples.hi: वह फ़िल्म के दौरान बोलता रहा।

common_mistake.wrong: Keep the phone on the table for one second.
common_mistake.right: Put the phone on the table for one second.
common_mistake.why: 'Keep' suggests leaving it there for a long time; 'put' is the single action.

cloze.sentence: ____ the receipt in case you need it.

en_def: to allow someone to do something
hi_nuance: 'Let' takes the base verb, no 'to': 'Let me go', not 'Let me to go'. 'Let's' means 'let us' and is a suggestion.

examples.en: Let me help you.
examples.hi: मुझे आपकी मदद करने दो।

examples.en: Let's go for a coffee.
examples.hi: चलो कॉफ़ी पीने चलते हैं।

examples.en: My parents let me stay out late.
examples.hi: मेरे माता-पिता मुझे देर तक बाहर रहने देते हैं।

examples.en: Don't let the dog in.
examples.hi: कुत्ते को अंदर मत आने दो।

examples.en: Let me know if you need anything.
examples.hi: अगर आपको कुछ चाहिए तो मुझे बताना।

common_mistake.wrong: Let me to check.
common_mistake.right: Let me check.
common_mistake.why: 'Let' is followed by the base verb without 'to'.

cloze.sentence: ____ me know when you're free.

en_def: to start doing something
hi_nuance: 'Begin' and 'start' are usually interchangeable; 'begin' is slightly more formal. Past is 'began', participle 'begun' — not 'beginned'.

examples.en: The class begins at nine.
examples.hi: कक्षा नौ बजे शुरू होती है।

examples.en: Let's begin with the first question.
examples.hi: चलो पहले सवाल से शुरू करते हैं।

examples.en: It began to rain.
examples.hi: बारिश होने लगी।

examples.en: She began learning English last year.
examples.hi: उसने पिछले साल अंग्रेज़ी सीखना शुरू किया।

examples.en: The film has already begun.
examples.hi: फ़िल्म पहले ही शुरू हो चुकी है।

common_mistake.wrong: The meeting was beginned late.
common_mistake.right: The meeting began late.
common_mistake.why: 'Begin' is irregular: begin, began, begun.

cloze.sentence: When does the show ____?

en_def: to make it easier for someone to do something
hi_nuance: 'Help' as a noun is uncountable: 'some help', not 'a help' or 'helps'. 'Help me to do' and 'help me do' are both correct.

examples.en: Can you help me with this?
examples.hi: क्या आप इसमें मेरी मदद कर सकते हैं?

examples.en: She helped me carry the bags.
examples.hi: उसने बैग उठाने में मेरी मदद की।

examples.en: Thanks for your help.
examples.hi: आपकी मदद के लिए धन्यवाद।

examples.en: This app helps you learn English.
examples.hi: यह ऐप आपको अंग्रेज़ी सीखने में मदद करता है।

examples.en: Help! I've lost my wallet.
examples.hi: बचाओ! मेरा बटुआ खो गया।

common_mistake.wrong: Please do a help for me.
common_mistake.right: Please help me.
common_mistake.why: 'Help' is used as a verb; 'do a help' is not English.

cloze.sentence: Could you ____ me with my homework?

en_def: to speak with someone
hi_nuance: The 'l' is silent: /tɔːk/. 'Talk to' and 'talk with' are both fine; 'talk about' a topic. Never 'talk in English' for a language — say 'speak English'.

examples.en: Can we talk for a minute?
examples.hi: क्या हम एक मिनट बात कर सकते हैं?

examples.en: She is talking to her manager.
examples.hi: वह अपने मैनेजर से बात कर रही है।

examples.en: We talked about the project.
examples.hi: हमने प्रोजेक्ट के बारे में बात की।

examples.en: He talks too much.
examples.hi: वह बहुत ज़्यादा बोलता है।

examples.en: Let's talk later.
examples.hi: बाद में बात करते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: Let us talk in English only.
common_mistake.right: Let's speak English only.
common_mistake.why: For languages, use 'speak', not 'talk in'.

cloze.sentence: I need to ____ to you about something.

en_def: to move around a point; to change direction; to become
hi_nuance: 'Turn on/off' is used for lights and devices — not 'open/close the light'. The vowel /ɜː/ is long, like 'bird'.

examples.en: Turn left at the signal.
examples.hi: सिग्नल पर बाएँ मुड़ो।

examples.en: Turn off the lights, please.
examples.hi: कृपया लाइट बंद कर दो।

examples.en: She turned around and smiled.
examples.hi: वह मुड़ी और मुस्कुराई।

examples.en: The leaves turn yellow in autumn.
examples.hi: पतझड़ में पत्ते पीले हो जाते हैं।

examples.en: He turned thirty last week.
examples.hi: वह पिछले हफ़्ते तीस साल का हो गया।

common_mistake.wrong: Open the fan, it's hot.
common_mistake.right: Turn on the fan, it's hot.
common_mistake.why: Devices are turned on/off, not opened/closed.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ down the volume.

en_def: to begin doing something; to make a machine work
hi_nuance: Do not add a vowel before 'st': it is 'start', not 'istart'. 'Start to' and 'start' + -ing are both correct.

examples.en: The meeting starts at ten.
examples.hi: मीटिंग दस बजे शुरू होती है।

examples.en: I started learning English in school.
examples.hi: मैंने स्कूल में अंग्रेज़ी सीखना शुरू किया।

examples.en: The car won't start.
examples.hi: गाड़ी स्टार्ट नहीं हो रही।

examples.en: Let's start again from the top.
examples.hi: चलो ऊपर से फिर शुरू करते हैं।

examples.en: She started her own business.
examples.hi: उसने अपना खुद का व्यवसाय शुरू किया।

common_mistake.wrong: We will start the meeting from ten.
common_mistake.right: We will start the meeting at ten.
common_mistake.why: A single point of time uses 'at', not 'from'.

cloze.sentence: What time does your shift ____?

en_def: to let someone see something; to explain how to do something
hi_nuance: 'Show me' takes the person first: 'Show me the photo', not 'Show the photo to me' (also correct but less common). Past participle 'shown'.

examples.en: Show me your ticket, please.
examples.hi: कृपया मुझे अपना टिकट दिखाइए।

examples.en: Can you show me how this works?
examples.hi: क्या आप मुझे दिखा सकते हैं कि यह कैसे काम करता है?

examples.en: The map shows the way to the hotel.
examples.hi: नक्शा होटल का रास्ता दिखाता है।

examples.en: She showed us around the city.
examples.hi: उसने हमें शहर घुमाया।

examples.en: The results show a clear improvement.
examples.hi: नतीजे साफ़ सुधार दिखाते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: He has showed me the file.
common_mistake.right: He has shown me the file.
common_mistake.why: The past participle of 'show' is 'shown'.

cloze.sentence: Let me ____ you the new office.

en_def: to notice a sound with your ears; to be told something
hi_nuance: 'Hear' is passive (sound reaches you); 'listen to' is active. 'I am hearing' is wrong — say 'I can hear'. 'Hear from someone' means receive a message.

examples.en: I can't hear you; the line is bad.
examples.hi: मुझे आपकी आवाज़ नहीं आ रही; लाइन खराब है।

examples.en: Did you hear that noise?
examples.hi: क्या आपने वह आवाज़ सुनी?

examples.en: I heard the news this morning.
examples.hi: मैंने आज सुबह ख़बर सुनी।

examples.en: Have you heard from Rahul lately?
examples.hi: क्या हाल में राहुल की कोई ख़बर मिली?

examples.en: She hears well for her age.
examples.hi: अपनी उम्र के हिसाब से वह अच्छा सुनती है।

common_mistake.wrong: I am not hearing you properly.
common_mistake.right: I can't hear you properly.
common_mistake.why: 'Hear' is a sense verb; use 'can hear', not the continuous.

cloze.sentence: Speak up, I can't ____ you.

en_def: to take part in a game or sport; to make music on an instrument
hi_nuance: Sports take no article ('play cricket'); instruments take 'the' ('play the guitar'). 'Play with' someone is for children; adults 'play against' or 'play tennis with'.

examples.en: We play cricket on Sundays.
examples.hi: हम रविवार को क्रिकेट खेलते हैं।

examples.en: She plays the piano beautifully.
examples.hi: वह बहुत सुंदर पियानो बजाती है।

examples.en: The children are playing outside.
examples.hi: बच्चे बाहर खेल रहे हैं।

examples.en: Play the video again.
examples.hi: वीडियो फिर से चलाओ।

examples.en: He played football for his college.
examples.hi: उसने अपने कॉलेज के लिए फ़ुटबॉल खेला।

common_mistake.wrong: I play the cricket every weekend.
common_mistake.right: I play cricket every weekend.
common_mistake.why: Sports and games take no article.

cloze.sentence: Do you ____ any musical instrument?

en_def: to move quickly on your feet; to manage; (of a machine or program) to operate
hi_nuance: In tech English, 'run a script' or 'the server is running' is standard. For businesses, 'run a shop' means manage it. Past: 'ran', participle 'run'.

examples.en: I run every morning.
examples.hi: मैं हर सुबह दौड़ता हूँ।

examples.en: She runs a small shop.
examples.hi: वह एक छोटी दुकान चलाती है।

examples.en: The program is running now.
examples.hi: प्रोग्राम अभी चल रहा है।

examples.en: He ran to catch the bus.
examples.hi: वह बस पकड़ने के लिए दौड़ा।

examples.en: Buses run every fifteen minutes.
examples.hi: बसें हर पंद्रह मिनट में चलती हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I runned the tests yesterday.
common_mistake.right: I ran the tests yesterday.
common_mistake.why: 'Run' is irregular: run, ran, run.

cloze.sentence: The kids ____ around the park all evening.

en_def: to change position or place; to change where you live
hi_nuance: Indian English says 'I shifted to Pune'; natural English is 'I moved to Pune'. 'Shift' is for work timings.

examples.en: Please move your car.
examples.hi: कृपया अपनी गाड़ी हटाइए।

examples.en: We moved to Bangalore last year.
examples.hi: हम पिछले साल बैंगलोर चले गए।

examples.en: Don't move; there's a bee on your arm.
examples.hi: हिलो मत; तुम्हारी बाँह पर मधुमक्खी है।

examples.en: The train started to move.
examples.hi: ट्रेन चलने लगी।

examples.en: Let's move to the next topic.
examples.hi: चलो अगले विषय पर चलते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: We shifted to a new flat.
common_mistake.right: We moved to a new flat.
common_mistake.why: 'Move' is the natural verb for changing home; 'shift' is Indian English.

cloze.sentence: Can you ____ a little to the left?

en_def: to enjoy or find something pleasant
hi_nuance: 'Like' is a state verb: 'I like tea', not 'I am liking tea'. 'Would like' is a polite way to say 'want': 'I would like some water'.

examples.en: I like spicy food.
examples.hi: मुझे मसालेदार खाना पसंद है।

examples.en: Do you like your new job?
examples.hi: क्या आपको अपनी नई नौकरी पसंद है?

examples.en: She likes reading at night.
examples.hi: उसे रात में पढ़ना पसंद है।

examples.en: I would like a coffee, please.
examples.hi: मुझे एक कॉफ़ी चाहिए, कृपया।

examples.en: They don't like cold weather.
examples.hi: उन्हें ठंडा मौसम पसंद नहीं है।

common_mistake.wrong: I am liking this song.
common_mistake.right: I like this song.
common_mistake.why: 'Like' is a state verb and is not used in the continuous.

cloze.sentence: Do you ____ Indian food?

en_def: to have your home in a place; to be alive
hi_nuance: The verb is /lɪv/ (short i); the adjective 'live' (a live show) is /laɪv/. Hindi speakers say 'I am living in Delhi' — for permanent homes use 'I live in Delhi'.

examples.en: I live in Ahmedabad.
examples.hi: मैं अहमदाबाद में रहता हूँ।

examples.en: Where do you live?
examples.hi: आप कहाँ रहते हैं?

examples.en: She lives with her parents.
examples.hi: वह अपने माता-पिता के साथ रहती है।

examples.en: My grandfather lived to ninety.
examples.hi: मेरे दादाजी नब्बे साल तक जिए।

examples.en: They are living in a hotel for now.
examples.hi: वे अभी के लिए एक होटल में रह रहे हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I am living in Surat since childhood.
common_mistake.right: I have lived in Surat since childhood.
common_mistake.why: 'Since' + start point needs the present perfect.

cloze.sentence: My sister ____ in Canada now.

en_def: to think that something is true
hi_nuance: 'Believe' = think it is true; 'believe in' = trust or have faith in. State verb: 'I believe', not 'I am believing'.

examples.en: I believe you.
examples.hi: मुझे आप पर विश्वास है।

examples.en: She believes in hard work.
examples.hi: वह मेहनत में विश्वास करती है।

examples.en: I can't believe it's already June.
examples.hi: मुझे यकीन नहीं हो रहा कि जून आ गया।

examples.en: Do you believe his story?
examples.hi: क्या आपको उसकी कहानी पर यकीन है?

examples.en: They believed the report was correct.
examples.hi: उन्हें लगा कि रिपोर्ट सही थी।

common_mistake.wrong: I am believing that it is true.
common_mistake.right: I believe that it is true.
common_mistake.why: 'Believe' is a state verb; use the simple form.

cloze.sentence: I ____ she will pass the exam.

en_def: to carry something to the place where the speaker is
hi_nuance: 'Bring' = toward the speaker; 'take' = away from the speaker. Hindi 'लाना/ले जाना' matches this well. Past: 'brought', not 'bringed'.

examples.en: Bring your laptop to the meeting.
examples.hi: मीटिंग में अपना लैपटॉप लाना।

examples.en: Can you bring me a glass of water?
examples.hi: क्या आप मुझे एक गिलास पानी ला सकते हैं?

examples.en: She brought her sister to the party.
examples.hi: वह अपनी बहन को पार्टी में लाई।

examples.en: I forgot to bring my ID.
examples.hi: मैं अपना आईडी लाना भूल गया।

examples.en: The rain brought some relief from the heat.
examples.hi: बारिश ने गर्मी से कुछ राहत दी।

common_mistake.wrong: I bringed the documents.
common_mistake.right: I brought the documents.
common_mistake.why: 'Bring' is irregular: bring, brought, brought.

cloze.sentence: Don't forget to ____ an umbrella.

en_def: to take place; to occur
hi_nuance: 'Happen' has no object and no passive: 'What happened?', not 'What was happened?'. 'Happen to' + verb = by chance: 'I happened to see him'.

examples.en: What happened to your phone?
examples.hi: आपके फ़ोन को क्या हुआ?

examples.en: Accidents happen.
examples.hi: दुर्घटनाएँ होती रहती हैं।

examples.en: It happened last night.
examples.hi: यह कल रात हुआ।

examples.en: Nothing happens in this town.
examples.hi: इस कस्बे में कुछ नहीं होता।

examples.en: I happened to meet her at the station.
examples.hi: संयोग से मैं उससे स्टेशन पर मिला।

common_mistake.wrong: What was happened yesterday?
common_mistake.right: What happened yesterday?
common_mistake.why: 'Happen' is never used in the passive.

cloze.sentence: Tell me exactly what ____ next.

en_def: to make letters or words on paper or a screen; to create a text
hi_nuance: The 'w' is silent. 'Write to me' (British) or 'write me' (American) both work. 'Write an exam' is Indian English — say 'take an exam'.

examples.en: Write your name here.
examples.hi: यहाँ अपना नाम लिखो।

examples.en: She writes a blog about food.
examples.hi: वह खाने के बारे में ब्लॉग लिखती है।

examples.en: I wrote him an email yesterday.
examples.hi: मैंने कल उसे एक ईमेल लिखा।

examples.en: He has written three reports this week.
examples.hi: उसने इस हफ़्ते तीन रिपोर्ट लिखी हैं।

examples.en: Please write clearly.
examples.hi: कृपया साफ़-साफ़ लिखें।

common_mistake.wrong: I wrote my exam last week.
common_mistake.right: I took my exam last week.
common_mistake.why: Exams are 'taken' or 'sat'; 'write an exam' is Indian English.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ your phone number on the form.

en_def: to rest your body on a chair or on the ground
hi_nuance: Short /ɪ/, not 'seat'. 'Sit down' is the action; 'be sitting' is the state. 'Sit for an exam' (British) is correct; 'sit in an exam' is not.

examples.en: Please sit down.
examples.hi: कृपया बैठिए।

examples.en: She is sitting by the window.
examples.hi: वह खिड़की के पास बैठी है।

examples.en: We sat on the floor and talked.
examples.hi: हम फ़र्श पर बैठकर बातें करते रहे।

examples.en: Sit here next to me.
examples.hi: यहाँ मेरे बगल में बैठो।

examples.en: I sat in the front row.
examples.hi: मैं आगे की पंक्ति में बैठा।

common_mistake.wrong: Take your sit, please.
common_mistake.right: Take your seat, please.
common_mistake.why: 'Seat' is the noun; 'sit' is the verb.

cloze.sentence: Come and ____ with us.

en_def: to be on your feet; to be in an upright position
hi_nuance: 'Can't stand' means 'hate': 'I can't stand traffic'. 'Stand up' is the action; 'be standing' is the state.

examples.en: Please stand up.
examples.hi: कृपया खड़े हो जाइए।

examples.en: He was standing near the door.
examples.hi: वह दरवाज़े के पास खड़ा था।

examples.en: We stood in the queue for an hour.
examples.hi: हम एक घंटे तक कतार में खड़े रहे।

examples.en: I can't stand this noise.
examples.hi: मैं यह शोर बर्दाश्त नहीं कर सकता।

examples.en: The bottle is standing on the shelf.
examples.hi: बोतल शेल्फ़ पर रखी है।

common_mistake.wrong: I standed there for one hour.
common_mistake.right: I stood there for an hour.
common_mistake.why: 'Stand' is irregular: stand, stood, stood.

cloze.sentence: Don't ____ in the doorway.

en_def: to no longer have something; to not win
hi_nuance: Spelling trap: 'lose' (verb, /luːz/) vs 'loose' (adjective, /luːs/, not tight). Many Indian learners write 'loose' when they mean 'lose'.

examples.en: I lost my keys again.
examples.hi: मैंने फिर से अपनी चाबियाँ खो दीं।

examples.en: Our team lost the match.
examples.hi: हमारी टीम मैच हार गई।

examples.en: Don't lose this document.
examples.hi: यह दस्तावेज़ मत खोना।

examples.en: She is losing weight.
examples.hi: उसका वज़न कम हो रहा है।

examples.en: He lost his job last month.
examples.hi: पिछले महीने उसकी नौकरी चली गई।

common_mistake.wrong: I don't want to loose my data.
common_mistake.right: I don't want to lose my data.
common_mistake.why: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not tight; the verb is 'lose'.

cloze.sentence: Be careful not to ____ your ticket.

en_def: to give money for something you buy or for work done
hi_nuance: 'Pay for' the thing you buy, 'pay' the person or the bill: 'pay for lunch', 'pay the waiter', 'pay the bill'. Past is 'paid', not 'payed'.

examples.en: I'll pay for dinner tonight.
examples.hi: आज रात के खाने के पैसे मैं दूँगा।

examples.en: Can I pay by card?
examples.hi: क्या मैं कार्ड से भुगतान कर सकता हूँ?

examples.en: She paid the electricity bill online.
examples.hi: उसने बिजली का बिल ऑनलाइन भरा।

examples.en: They pay their staff on the first of the month.
examples.hi: वे महीने की पहली तारीख़ को अपने कर्मचारियों को वेतन देते हैं।

examples.en: How much did you pay for this phone?
examples.hi: आपने इस फ़ोन के लिए कितने पैसे दिए?

common_mistake.wrong: I payed the rent yesterday.
common_mistake.right: I paid the rent yesterday.
common_mistake.why: 'Pay' is irregular: pay, paid, paid.

cloze.sentence: Who is going to ____ for the tickets?

en_def: to come together with someone; to see someone for the first time
hi_nuance: 'Meet' takes a person directly: 'meet him', not 'meet with him' (unless a formal meeting). Hindi 'मिलना' for receiving things is 'get', not 'meet'.

examples.en: Nice to meet you.
examples.hi: आपसे मिलकर खुशी हुई।

examples.en: Let's meet at the café at five.
examples.hi: चलो पाँच बजे कैफ़े में मिलते हैं।

examples.en: I met my wife at college.
examples.hi: मैं अपनी पत्नी से कॉलेज में मिला था।

examples.en: Have you met the new manager?
examples.hi: क्या आप नए मैनेजर से मिले हैं?

examples.en: We meet every Friday for lunch.
examples.hi: हम हर शुक्रवार को लंच पर मिलते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I met a good job last month.
common_mistake.right: I got a good job last month.
common_mistake.why: 'Meet' is for people; things are 'got' or 'found'.

cloze.sentence: Where shall we ____ tomorrow?

en_def: to contain something as a part of a whole
hi_nuance: 'Including' introduces examples: 'many tools, including Burp'. Hindi speakers sometimes say 'inclusive of' where 'including' is simpler and better.

examples.en: The price includes breakfast.
examples.hi: कीमत में नाश्ता शामिल है।

examples.en: Does the ticket include a meal?
examples.hi: क्या टिकट में खाना शामिल है?

examples.en: Please include your phone number.
examples.hi: कृपया अपना फ़ोन नंबर शामिल करें।

examples.en: The team includes two designers.
examples.hi: टीम में दो डिज़ाइनर शामिल हैं।

examples.en: Everyone came, including my boss.
examples.hi: सब आए, मेरे बॉस समेत।

common_mistake.wrong: The fee is inclusive of the taxes.
common_mistake.right: The fee includes taxes.
common_mistake.why: 'Includes' is the natural verb; 'inclusive of' is stiff and formal.

cloze.sentence: Does the rent ____ electricity?

en_def: to keep doing something; to start again after a pause
hi_nuance: Stress the second syllable: con-TI-nue. 'Continue to do' and 'continue doing' are both correct. Don't say 'continue on' — just 'continue'.

examples.en: Please continue; I'm listening.
examples.hi: कृपया जारी रखिए; मैं सुन रहा हूँ।

examples.en: The rain continued all night.
examples.hi: बारिश पूरी रात जारी रही।

examples.en: She continued working after the baby was born.
examples.hi: बच्चे के जन्म के बाद उसने काम करना जारी रखा।

examples.en: We will continue the meeting after lunch.
examples.hi: हम लंच के बाद मीटिंग जारी रखेंगे।

examples.en: Prices continue to rise.
examples.hi: कीमतें बढ़ती जा रही हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: Let us continue on with the lesson.
common_mistake.right: Let's continue with the lesson.
common_mistake.why: 'Continue on' is redundant; 'continue with' is enough.

cloze.sentence: Shall we ____ from where we stopped?

en_def: to put something in a place or position; to fix a time, price, or level
hi_nuance: 'Set an alarm', 'set a date', 'set a password' — these fixed phrases are more natural than 'keep an alarm' or 'put a password'.

examples.en: Set the alarm for six.
examples.hi: अलार्म छह बजे का लगाओ।

examples.en: Have you set a date for the wedding?
examples.hi: क्या आपने शादी की तारीख़ तय कर ली है?

examples.en: She set the vase on the table.
examples.hi: उसने फूलदान मेज़ पर रखा।

examples.en: The sun sets around seven.
examples.hi: सूरज लगभग सात बजे डूबता है।

examples.en: The manager set a new target.
examples.hi: मैनेजर ने एक नया लक्ष्य तय किया।

common_mistake.wrong: I kept an alarm for five o'clock.
common_mistake.right: I set an alarm for five o'clock.
common_mistake.why: Alarms are 'set', not 'kept'.

cloze.sentence: Let's ____ a time for the next call.

en_def: to get knowledge or skill by studying or practising
hi_nuance: 'Learn' = gain the skill; 'study' = the activity. 'I learnt English for two years' means you got it; 'I studied English for two years' is the effort. Long vowel /ɜː/.

examples.en: I am learning English online.
examples.hi: मैं ऑनलाइन अंग्रेज़ी सीख रहा हूँ।

examples.en: Children learn languages quickly.
examples.hi: बच्चे भाषाएँ जल्दी सीखते हैं।

examples.en: She learnt to drive last year.
examples.hi: उसने पिछले साल गाड़ी चलाना सीखा।

examples.en: We learn from our mistakes.
examples.hi: हम अपनी गलतियों से सीखते हैं।

examples.en: What did you learn today?
examples.hi: आज आपने क्या सीखा?

common_mistake.wrong: I am learning English since two years.
common_mistake.right: I have been learning English for two years.
common_mistake.why: A duration uses 'for', and needs the present perfect continuous.

cloze.sentence: It takes time to ____ a new language.

en_def: to become different; to make something different; to exchange
hi_nuance: 'Change' (money you get back) is uncountable: 'Keep the change'. 'Change into' clothes; 'change trains'; 'change your mind'.

examples.en: The weather changed suddenly.
examples.hi: मौसम अचानक बदल गया।

examples.en: I need to change my password.
examples.hi: मुझे अपना पासवर्ड बदलना है।

examples.en: She changed her mind about the trip.
examples.hi: उसने यात्रा के बारे में अपना मन बदल लिया।

examples.en: We have to change trains at Surat.
examples.hi: हमें सूरत में ट्रेन बदलनी होगी।

examples.en: Do you have change for a hundred?
examples.hi: क्या आपके पास सौ के छुट्टे हैं?

common_mistake.wrong: There are many changes in the plan, please revert back.
common_mistake.right: There are many changes in the plan; please reply.
common_mistake.why: 'Revert back' is an Indianism; 'reply' or 'get back to me' is natural.

cloze.sentence: You should ____ your password every few months.

en_def: to guide or be in charge of a group; to go in front; to result in
hi_def: नेतृत्व करना; ले जाना; कारण बनना
hi_nuance: Verb /liːd/ (past 'led', /led/). The metal 'lead' is /led/. 'Lead to' = cause: 'Stress leads to mistakes'. Don't write 'lead' for the past tense.

examples.en: She leads a team of ten engineers.
examples.hi: वह दस इंजीनियरों की टीम का नेतृत्व करती है।

examples.en: This road leads to the station.
examples.hi: यह सड़क स्टेशन तक जाती है।

examples.en: Poor sleep can lead to mistakes.
examples.hi: कम नींद गलतियों का कारण बन सकती है।

examples.en: He led the meeting very well.
examples.hi: उसने मीटिंग बहुत अच्छी तरह चलाई।

examples.en: Who is leading the project now?
examples.hi: अब प्रोजेक्ट का नेतृत्व कौन कर रहा है?

common_mistake.wrong: He lead the team last year.
common_mistake.right: He led the team last year.
common_mistake.why: The past tense of 'lead' is spelt 'led'.

cloze.sentence: Bad passwords often ____ to security problems.

en_def: to know the meaning of something; to know how someone feels
hi_nuance: State verb — never 'I am understanding'. Also 'understood' works as a short reply. Avoid the Indianism 'I am not getting' in formal contexts.

examples.en: I don't understand this question.
examples.hi: मुझे यह सवाल समझ नहीं आ रहा।

examples.en: Do you understand Gujarati?
examples.hi: क्या आप गुजराती समझते हैं?

examples.en: She understood the problem immediately.
examples.hi: उसने तुरंत समस्या समझ ली।

examples.en: Now I understand why he left.
examples.hi: अब मैं समझ गया कि वह क्यों गया।

examples.en: I understand how you feel.
examples.hi: मैं समझता हूँ आप कैसा महसूस कर रहे हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I am not understanding the requirement.
common_mistake.right: I don't understand the requirement.
common_mistake.why: 'Understand' is a state verb; use the simple form.

cloze.sentence: Sorry, I didn't ____ what you said.

en_def: to look at something for a period of time, especially something moving
hi_nuance: 'Watch' for TV, films, matches — things that move. 'See' a film at the cinema is also fine, but 'see TV' is wrong: 'watch TV'.

examples.en: I watch the news every evening.
examples.hi: मैं हर शाम समाचार देखता हूँ।

examples.en: Did you watch the match?
examples.hi: क्या आपने मैच देखा?

examples.en: Watch your step; the floor is wet.
examples.hi: संभलकर चलो; फ़र्श गीला है।

examples.en: She is watching a film on her tablet.
examples.hi: वह अपने टैबलेट पर फ़िल्म देख रही है।

examples.en: Can you watch my bag for a minute?
examples.hi: क्या आप एक मिनट मेरे बैग का ध्यान रख सकते हैं?

common_mistake.wrong: I see TV every night.
common_mistake.right: I watch TV every night.
common_mistake.why: 'Watch' is used for TV and moving images.

cloze.sentence: Let's ____ a movie tonight.

en_def: to go after someone; to obey or act according to; to understand
hi_nuance: 'Follow' takes a direct object: 'follow the rules', not 'follow to the rules'. 'Do you follow?' means 'Do you understand?'.

examples.en: Follow me; I'll show you the way.
examples.hi: मेरे पीछे आइए; मैं आपको रास्ता दिखाऊँगा।

examples.en: Please follow the instructions carefully.
examples.hi: कृपया निर्देशों का ध्यान से पालन करें।

examples.en: The dog followed him home.
examples.hi: कुत्ता उसके पीछे-पीछे घर तक आया।

examples.en: I follow her on Instagram.
examples.hi: मैं इंस्टाग्राम पर उसे फ़ॉलो करता हूँ।

examples.en: Sorry, I don't follow you.
examples.hi: माफ़ कीजिए, मैं आपकी बात समझ नहीं पाया।

common_mistake.wrong: Please follow to the steps below.
common_mistake.right: Please follow the steps below.
common_mistake.why: 'Follow' takes its object directly, without 'to'.

cloze.sentence: Just ____ the signs to the exit.

en_def: to end a movement or action; to prevent
hi_nuance: 'Stop doing' = end the action ('stop smoking'); 'stop to do' = pause in order to do ('stop to buy milk'). These mean different things.

examples.en: Stop the car here.
examples.hi: गाड़ी यहाँ रोको।

examples.en: The rain has stopped.
examples.hi: बारिश रुक गई है।

examples.en: Please stop talking during the film.
examples.hi: कृपया फ़िल्म के दौरान बात करना बंद करें।

examples.en: We stopped to have tea on the way.
examples.hi: हम रास्ते में चाय पीने के लिए रुके।

examples.en: The bus stops outside my house.
examples.hi: बस मेरे घर के बाहर रुकती है।

common_mistake.wrong: He stopped to smoke last year.
common_mistake.right: He stopped smoking last year.
common_mistake.why: 'Stop' + -ing means quit; 'stop to' means pause in order to do it.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ at the next petrol station.

en_def: to make something new exist
hi_nuance: Stress on the second syllable: cre-ATE. In tech, 'create an account/file/ticket' is standard; 'make an account' sounds childish.

examples.en: Create a new account to continue.
examples.hi: जारी रखने के लिए एक नया खाता बनाएँ।

examples.en: She created a website for her shop.
examples.hi: उसने अपनी दुकान के लिए एक वेबसाइट बनाई।

examples.en: The new factory will create jobs.
examples.hi: नया कारखाना नौकरियाँ पैदा करेगा।

examples.en: Who created this file?
examples.hi: यह फ़ाइल किसने बनाई?

examples.en: Too many alerts create confusion.
examples.hi: बहुत ज़्यादा अलर्ट भ्रम पैदा करते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: Please make one ticket for this issue.
common_mistake.right: Please create a ticket for this issue.
common_mistake.why: 'Create' is the standard verb for tickets, accounts and files; 'one' is not an article.

cloze.sentence: You need to ____ a strong password.

en_def: to say words; to be able to use a language
hi_nuance: Use 'speak' for languages ('speak English') and 'talk' for conversations. No vowel before 'sp': it is 'speak', not 'ispeak'. Past: 'spoke', participle 'spoken'.

examples.en: Do you speak Hindi?
examples.hi: क्या आप हिन्दी बोलते हैं?

examples.en: Can I speak to the manager?
examples.hi: क्या मैं मैनेजर से बात कर सकता हूँ?

examples.en: She speaks three languages.
examples.hi: वह तीन भाषाएँ बोलती है।

examples.en: He spoke very quietly.
examples.hi: वह बहुत धीमे बोला।

examples.en: We haven't spoken since March.
examples.hi: हमने मार्च से बात नहीं की है।

common_mistake.wrong: I can talk English but not fluently.
common_mistake.right: I can speak English but not fluently.
common_mistake.why: For languages, use 'speak'.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ slowly; I am still learning.

en_def: to look at words and understand them
hi_nuance: Present 'read' is /riːd/; past 'read' is /red/ — same spelling. Hindi 'पढ़ना' also means 'study'; for that use 'study', not 'read': 'I studied engineering'.

examples.en: I read the newspaper every morning.
examples.hi: मैं हर सुबह अख़बार पढ़ता हूँ।

examples.en: Have you read this book?
examples.hi: क्या आपने यह किताब पढ़ी है?

examples.en: She read the email twice.
examples.hi: उसने ईमेल दो बार पढ़ा।

examples.en: Read the instructions before you start.
examples.hi: शुरू करने से पहले निर्देश पढ़ें।

examples.en: My son is learning to read.
examples.hi: मेरा बेटा पढ़ना सीख रहा है।

common_mistake.wrong: I read engineering in Pune.
common_mistake.right: I studied engineering in Pune.
common_mistake.why: Hindi 'पढ़ना' covers both, but English uses 'study' for a degree subject.

cloze.sentence: Did you ____ the report I sent?

en_def: to use money or time on something
hi_nuance: 'Spend time doing' — not 'spend time to do' or 'spend time in doing'. Past: 'spent', not 'spended'.

examples.en: I spent too much money this month.
examples.hi: मैंने इस महीने बहुत ज़्यादा पैसा खर्च कर दिया।

examples.en: We spent the weekend in Udaipur.
examples.hi: हमने वीकेंड उदयपुर में बिताया।

examples.en: How much time do you spend on social media?
examples.hi: आप सोशल मीडिया पर कितना समय बिताते हैं?

examples.en: She spends hours reading.
examples.hi: वह घंटों पढ़ने में बिताती है।

examples.en: Don't spend it all at once.
examples.hi: सब एक साथ खर्च मत करो।

common_mistake.wrong: I spent two hours in doing the report.
common_mistake.right: I spent two hours doing the report.
common_mistake.why: 'Spend time' is followed directly by the -ing form.

cloze.sentence: How much did you ____ on the laptop?

en_def: to become bigger or develop; to plant and look after
hi_nuance: 'Grow up' = become an adult; 'grow' = increase in size. 'Grown up' is the adjective. Vowel is /əʊ/ as in 'go', not 'graw'.

examples.en: My father grows vegetables in the garden.
examples.hi: मेरे पिताजी बगीचे में सब्ज़ियाँ उगाते हैं।

examples.en: Children grow so fast.
examples.hi: बच्चे बहुत तेज़ी से बढ़ते हैं।

examples.en: The company is growing quickly.
examples.hi: कंपनी तेज़ी से बढ़ रही है।

examples.en: I grew up in a small village.
examples.hi: मैं एक छोटे गाँव में बड़ा हुआ।

examples.en: Rice grows well in wet areas.
examples.hi: धान गीले इलाकों में अच्छा उगता है।

common_mistake.wrong: I was grown up in Rajkot.
common_mistake.right: I grew up in Rajkot.
common_mistake.why: 'Grow up' is active; there is no passive form for it.

cloze.sentence: These plants ____ best in the sun.

en_def: to move something so it is no longer closed; to start a business or file
hi_nuance: Doors, windows, files, shops and accounts 'open'. Lights, fans and taps do not — they are 'turned on'. 'Open' is also the adjective: 'the shop is open'.

examples.en: Open the window; it's hot.
examples.hi: खिड़की खोलो; गर्मी है।

examples.en: What time does the bank open?
examples.hi: बैंक कितने बजे खुलता है?

examples.en: She opened the email and read it.
examples.hi: उसने ईमेल खोला और पढ़ा।

examples.en: They opened a new branch in Surat.
examples.hi: उन्होंने सूरत में नई शाखा खोली।

examples.en: The shop is open until nine.
examples.hi: दुकान नौ बजे तक खुली है।

common_mistake.wrong: Open the fan, please.
common_mistake.right: Turn on the fan, please.
common_mistake.why: Devices are turned on, not opened.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ your books to page ten.

en_def: to move on foot at a normal speed
hi_nuance: The 'l' is silent: /wɔːk/. 'Go for a walk' is the noun. 'Walk to work' = go on foot; Hindi speakers sometimes say 'go by walk' — say 'walk' or 'go on foot'.

examples.en: I walk to work every day.
examples.hi: मैं रोज़ पैदल काम पर जाता हूँ।

examples.en: Let's walk; it's not far.
examples.hi: चलो पैदल चलते हैं; दूर नहीं है।

examples.en: She walks her dog in the evening.
examples.hi: वह शाम को अपने कुत्ते को घुमाती है।

examples.en: We walked along the beach.
examples.hi: हम समुद्र तट के किनारे चले।

examples.en: The baby has started to walk.
examples.hi: बच्चे ने चलना शुरू कर दिया है।

common_mistake.wrong: I go to office by walk.
common_mistake.right: I walk to the office.
common_mistake.why: 'By walk' is not English; use the verb 'walk' or 'on foot'.

cloze.sentence: It's a nice day, so let's ____ to the park.

en_def: to be the best or first in a game, race, or competition
hi_nuance: You 'win' a match or a prize, but you 'beat' a person or team: 'We beat Australia', not 'We won Australia'. Past: 'won' (/wʌn/).

examples.en: India won the match by ten runs.
examples.hi: भारत ने दस रन से मैच जीता।

examples.en: Who won the election?
examples.hi: चुनाव किसने जीता?

examples.en: She won first prize in the competition.
examples.hi: उसने प्रतियोगिता में पहला पुरस्कार जीता।

examples.en: You can't win every time.
examples.hi: आप हर बार नहीं जीत सकते।

examples.en: They have won three games in a row.
examples.hi: उन्होंने लगातार तीन खेल जीते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: We won Pakistan in the final.
common_mistake.right: We beat Pakistan in the final.
common_mistake.why: You 'win' a game but 'beat' an opponent.

cloze.sentence: I hope our team will ____ tonight.

en_def: to give lessons; to show someone how to do something
hi_nuance: 'Teach' someone something / to do something. Hindi 'पढ़ाना' can be 'teach'; 'सिखाना' is also 'teach'. Past: 'taught' (/tɔːt/), not 'teached'.

examples.en: She teaches maths at a school.
examples.hi: वह एक स्कूल में गणित पढ़ाती है।

examples.en: My father taught me to swim.
examples.hi: मेरे पिताजी ने मुझे तैरना सिखाया।

examples.en: Can you teach me this game?
examples.hi: क्या आप मुझे यह खेल सिखा सकते हैं?

examples.en: Experience teaches you a lot.
examples.hi: अनुभव आपको बहुत कुछ सिखाता है।

examples.en: He has taught English for ten years.
examples.hi: उसने दस साल तक अंग्रेज़ी पढ़ाई है।

common_mistake.wrong: He teached us grammar.
common_mistake.right: He taught us grammar.
common_mistake.why: 'Teach' is irregular: teach, taught, taught.

cloze.sentence: Who will ____ the new batch?

en_def: to say you will give or do something if the other person wants it
hi_def: पेश करना, देने की बात कहना
hi_nuance: 'Offer' someone something: 'She offered me tea'. 'Offer to do': 'He offered to help'. As a noun, 'a job offer'.

examples.en: She offered me a cup of tea.
examples.hi: उसने मुझे एक कप चाय देने को कहा।

examples.en: He offered to drive us home.
examples.hi: उसने हमें घर छोड़ने की पेशकश की।

examples.en: The company offered him a job.
examples.hi: कंपनी ने उसे नौकरी की पेशकश की।

examples.en: They are offering a discount this week.
examples.hi: वे इस हफ़्ते छूट दे रहे हैं।

examples.en: Thanks for the offer, but I'm fine.
examples.hi: पेशकश के लिए धन्यवाद, पर मैं ठीक हूँ।

common_mistake.wrong: He offered for helping me.
common_mistake.right: He offered to help me.
common_mistake.why: 'Offer' is followed by 'to' + verb.

cloze.sentence: Did they ____ you the job?

en_def: to keep something in your memory; to bring it back to mind
hi_nuance: 'Remember to do' = don't forget a duty; 'remember doing' = have a memory of it. State verb — 'I am remembering' is wrong. Hindi 'याद आना' → 'I remember', not 'It comes to my memory'.

examples.en: I can't remember his name.
examples.hi: मुझे उसका नाम याद नहीं आ रहा।

examples.en: Remember to lock the door.
examples.hi: दरवाज़ा बंद करना याद रखना।

examples.en: Do you remember our first meeting?
examples.hi: क्या आपको हमारी पहली मुलाक़ात याद है?

examples.en: She remembered everything he said.
examples.hi: उसे उसकी कही हर बात याद थी।

examples.en: I remember visiting this place as a child.
examples.hi: मुझे बचपन में इस जगह आना याद है।

common_mistake.wrong: I am not remembering the password.
common_mistake.right: I don't remember the password.
common_mistake.why: 'Remember' is a state verb; use the simple form.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ to send me the file.

en_def: to think carefully about something before deciding
hi_nuance: 'Consider' + -ing: 'consider moving', not 'consider to move'. Stress on the second syllable: con-SI-der.

examples.en: We are considering a new office.
examples.hi: हम एक नए ऑफ़िस के बारे में विचार कर रहे हैं।

examples.en: Have you considered working abroad?
examples.hi: क्या आपने विदेश में काम करने के बारे में सोचा है?

examples.en: Please consider my request.
examples.hi: कृपया मेरे अनुरोध पर विचार करें।

examples.en: I consider him a good friend.
examples.hi: मैं उसे एक अच्छा दोस्त मानता हूँ।

examples.en: All things considered, it went well.
examples.hi: सब कुछ देखते हुए, यह अच्छा रहा।

common_mistake.wrong: I am considering to buy a bike.
common_mistake.right: I am considering buying a bike.
common_mistake.why: 'Consider' is followed by the -ing form.

cloze.sentence: You should ____ all the options first.

en_def: to become visible; to seem
hi_nuance: Indian English uses 'appear for an exam' — natural English is 'take an exam' or 'sit an exam'. 'Appear to be' = seem to be.

examples.en: A message appeared on the screen.
examples.hi: स्क्रीन पर एक संदेश दिखाई दिया।

examples.en: He appeared tired after the trip.
examples.hi: यात्रा के बाद वह थका हुआ लग रहा था।

examples.en: The sun appeared from behind the clouds.
examples.hi: सूरज बादलों के पीछे से निकला।

examples.en: It appears that the server is down.
examples.hi: लगता है कि सर्वर बंद है।

examples.en: She suddenly appeared at the door.
examples.hi: वह अचानक दरवाज़े पर आ गई।

common_mistake.wrong: I appeared for the interview yesterday.
common_mistake.right: I had my interview yesterday.
common_mistake.why: 'Appear for' is Indian English; say 'have' an interview or 'take' an exam.

cloze.sentence: An error ____ every time I click the button.

en_def: to get something by paying money
hi_nuance: Same sound as 'by' and 'bye'. Past 'bought' (/bɔːt/) — not 'buyed'. 'Buy from' a shop, 'buy for' someone.

examples.en: I bought a new phone yesterday.
examples.hi: मैंने कल एक नया फ़ोन खरीदा।

examples.en: Where did you buy this shirt?
examples.hi: आपने यह शर्ट कहाँ से खरीदी?

examples.en: We need to buy some vegetables.
examples.hi: हमें कुछ सब्ज़ियाँ खरीदनी हैं।

examples.en: She buys her clothes online.
examples.hi: वह अपने कपड़े ऑनलाइन खरीदती है।

examples.en: Can you buy me a coffee?
examples.hi: क्या आप मुझे एक कॉफ़ी खरीद कर दे सकते हैं?

common_mistake.wrong: I buyed this from Amazon.
common_mistake.right: I bought this from Amazon.
common_mistake.why: 'Buy' is irregular: buy, bought, bought.

cloze.sentence: I want to ____ a gift for my mother.

en_def: to give food or drink to someone; to work for; to be useful for a purpose
hi_nuance: 'Serve' the customer, 'serve' food. In tech, 'the server serves the page'. Long /ɜː/ vowel, /v/ with the teeth on the lip.

examples.en: Dinner is served at eight.
examples.hi: रात का खाना आठ बजे परोसा जाता है।

examples.en: This restaurant serves great dosa.
examples.hi: यह रेस्तराँ बढ़िया डोसा परोसता है।

examples.en: He served in the army for ten years.
examples.hi: उसने दस साल सेना में सेवा की।

examples.en: Are you being served?
examples.hi: क्या कोई आपकी मदद कर रहा है?

examples.en: This box serves as a table.
examples.hi: यह डिब्बा मेज़ के काम आता है।

common_mistake.wrong: They serve the breakfast from seven.
common_mistake.right: They serve breakfast from seven.
common_mistake.why: Meals take no article.

cloze.sentence: Do they ____ vegetarian food here?

en_def: to stop living
hi_nuance: Indian English often uses 'expired' for people; natural English is 'passed away' (polite) or 'died'. 'Die of' an illness, 'die in' an accident. The noun is 'death', the adjective 'dead'.

examples.en: His grandfather died last year.
examples.hi: उसके दादाजी पिछले साल गुज़र गए।

examples.en: Many people die of heart disease.
examples.hi: बहुत से लोग दिल की बीमारी से मरते हैं।

examples.en: The plant died because nobody watered it.
examples.hi: पौधा इसलिए मर गया क्योंकि किसी ने पानी नहीं दिया।

examples.en: My phone battery is dying.
examples.hi: मेरे फ़ोन की बैटरी ख़त्म हो रही है।

examples.en: I'm dying to see the new film.
examples.hi: मैं नई फ़िल्म देखने के लिए बेताब हूँ।

common_mistake.wrong: My uncle expired last month.
common_mistake.right: My uncle passed away last month.
common_mistake.why: 'Expire' is used for passports and licences; for people, say 'pass away' or 'die'.

cloze.sentence: Plants ____ without water.

en_def: to make something go to another place, especially by post or online
hi_nuance: 'Send someone something' or 'send something to someone'. Past 'sent', not 'sended'. Don't say 'send me the same' — say 'send it to me'.

examples.en: I sent you an email this morning.
examples.hi: मैंने आज सुबह आपको एक ईमेल भेजा।

examples.en: Please send me the report by Friday.
examples.hi: कृपया मुझे शुक्रवार तक रिपोर्ट भेजें।

examples.en: She sends money home every month.
examples.hi: वह हर महीने घर पैसे भेजती है।

examples.en: Did you send the invitation to everyone?
examples.hi: क्या आपने सबको निमंत्रण भेजा?

examples.en: They sent their son to a good school.
examples.hi: उन्होंने अपने बेटे को अच्छे स्कूल में भेजा।

common_mistake.wrong: Kindly send me the same.
common_mistake.right: Please send it to me.
common_mistake.why: 'The same' as a pronoun and 'kindly' are Indianisms; 'please send it' is natural.

cloze.sentence: Could you ____ me the address?

en_def: to make something by putting parts together
hi_nuance: The 'u' is silent: /bɪld/. Past 'built'. In tech 'build' is also a noun: 'the latest build'. 'Build a house/app/team/career'.

examples.en: They are building a new bridge.
examples.hi: वे एक नया पुल बना रहे हैं।

examples.en: My uncle built this house in 1990.
examples.hi: मेरे चाचा ने यह घर 1990 में बनाया था।

examples.en: We built the app in three months.
examples.hi: हमने तीन महीने में ऐप बनाया।

examples.en: It takes years to build trust.
examples.hi: भरोसा बनाने में सालों लगते हैं।

examples.en: She is building a strong team.
examples.hi: वह एक मज़बूत टीम बना रही है।

common_mistake.wrong: The house was builded last year.
common_mistake.right: The house was built last year.
common_mistake.why: 'Build' is irregular: build, built, built.

cloze.sentence: They plan to ____ a school here.

en_def: to remain in a place or condition; to live somewhere for a short time
hi_nuance: Indian English uses 'stay' for permanent homes ('I stay in Delhi'); natural English uses 'live' for that and 'stay' for short visits or hotels.

examples.en: We stayed at a hotel near the beach.
examples.hi: हम समुद्र तट के पास एक होटल में ठहरे।

examples.en: Please stay here until I come back.
examples.hi: कृपया मेरे वापस आने तक यहाँ रुकिए।

examples.en: Stay calm and call for help.
examples.hi: शांत रहो और मदद के लिए फ़ोन करो।

examples.en: How long are you staying in Mumbai?
examples.hi: आप मुंबई में कितने दिन रुकेंगे?

examples.en: I stayed up late to finish the work.
examples.hi: मैं काम ख़त्म करने के लिए देर तक जागा।

common_mistake.wrong: I stay in Ahmedabad with my family.
common_mistake.right: I live in Ahmedabad with my family.
common_mistake.why: 'Live' is for your permanent home; 'stay' is for short visits.

cloze.sentence: Where did you ____ during your trip?

en_def: to drop down from a higher place; to decrease
hi_nuance: 'Fall' has no object; 'drop' can have one: 'I dropped the phone' vs 'The phone fell'. 'Fall down' is used for people. Past: 'fell', participle 'fallen'.

examples.en: Be careful, or you'll fall.
examples.hi: सावधान रहो, नहीं तो गिर जाओगे।

examples.en: The leaves fall in October.
examples.hi: अक्टूबर में पत्ते गिरते हैं।

examples.en: Prices have fallen this year.
examples.hi: इस साल कीमतें गिरी हैं।

examples.en: She fell and hurt her knee.
examples.hi: वह गिरी और उसके घुटने में चोट लगी।

examples.en: I fell asleep during the film.
examples.hi: मैं फ़िल्म के दौरान सो गया।

common_mistake.wrong: I fell down my phone.
common_mistake.right: I dropped my phone.
common_mistake.why: 'Fall' cannot take an object; use 'drop' when you let something fall.

cloze.sentence: Temperatures ____ sharply at night in the desert.

en_def: to divide or open something with a knife or sharp tool; to reduce
hi_nuance: Vowel /ʌ/ as in 'but', not 'cart'. Past and participle are also 'cut'. Indian English 'cut the call' → natural English 'hang up' or 'end the call'.

examples.en: Cut the onions into small pieces.
examples.hi: प्याज़ को छोटे टुकड़ों में काटो।

examples.en: I cut my finger while cooking.
examples.hi: खाना बनाते समय मेरी उँगली कट गई।

examples.en: The company cut its prices by ten percent.
examples.hi: कंपनी ने अपनी कीमतें दस प्रतिशत घटा दीं।

examples.en: He cut his hair short.
examples.hi: उसने अपने बाल छोटे करवा लिए।

examples.en: Can you cut this cake for everyone?
examples.hi: क्या आप सबके लिए यह केक काट सकते हैं?

common_mistake.wrong: He cut the call suddenly.
common_mistake.right: He hung up suddenly.
common_mistake.why: 'Cut the call' is Indian English; 'hang up' is natural.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ the paper along the line.

en_def: to arrive at a place; to stretch out your hand to touch or get something
hi_nuance: 'Reach' takes the place directly: 'reach the station', not 'reach to the station'. Indian English 'I reached' (with no place) → say 'I've arrived' or 'I'm here'.

examples.en: We reached the airport at six.
examples.hi: हम छह बजे हवाई अड्डे पहुँचे।

examples.en: Can you reach the top shelf?
examples.hi: क्या आपका हाथ ऊपर वाली शेल्फ़ तक पहुँचता है?

examples.en: Call me when you reach home.
examples.hi: घर पहुँचकर मुझे फ़ोन करना।

examples.en: The message didn't reach him in time.
examples.hi: संदेश समय पर उस तक नहीं पहुँचा।

examples.en: She reached out and took my hand.
examples.hi: उसने हाथ बढ़ाकर मेरा हाथ पकड़ा।

common_mistake.wrong: I reached to the office at ten.
common_mistake.right: I reached the office at ten.
common_mistake.why: 'Reach' takes its object directly, without 'to'.

cloze.sentence: What time will we ____ Jaipur?

en_def: to cause someone or something to die; to stop a process
hi_nuance: In tech English, 'kill a process' is standard and not violent. 'Kill time' means pass time while waiting. Short /ɪ/ vowel.

examples.en: The cold killed all the plants.
examples.hi: ठंड ने सभी पौधों को मार दिया।

examples.en: Please don't kill the spider; put it outside.
examples.hi: कृपया मकड़ी को मत मारो; उसे बाहर रख दो।

examples.en: I killed the process from the terminal.
examples.hi: मैंने टर्मिनल से प्रक्रिया बंद कर दी।

examples.en: We killed time by playing cards.
examples.hi: हमने ताश खेलकर समय बिताया।

examples.en: Smoking kills.
examples.hi: धूम्रपान जानलेवा है।

common_mistake.wrong: The mosquito bited me, so I killed it.
common_mistake.right: The mosquito bit me, so I killed it.
common_mistake.why: 'Bite' is irregular: bite, bit, bitten.

cloze.sentence: You can ____ the app if it freezes.

en_def: to stay in the same place or condition; to be left after others have gone
hi_nuance: 'Remain' is more formal than 'stay'. 'Remaining' means left over: 'the remaining files'. Stress the second syllable: re-MAIN.

examples.en: Please remain seated until the plane stops.
examples.hi: कृपया विमान के रुकने तक बैठे रहें।

examples.en: Only two tickets remain.
examples.hi: सिर्फ़ दो टिकट बचे हैं।

examples.en: The shop remained closed on Monday.
examples.hi: दुकान सोमवार को बंद रही।

examples.en: He remained silent during the meeting.
examples.hi: वह मीटिंग के दौरान चुप रहा।

examples.en: The remaining work will be done tomorrow.
examples.hi: बचा हुआ काम कल किया जाएगा।

common_mistake.wrong: How much balance is remaining?
common_mistake.right: How much is left?
common_mistake.why: 'Balance is remaining' is Indian English; 'left' is the natural word.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ calm during the drill.

en_def: the passing of hours and days; a particular moment; an occasion
hi_nuance: 'Time' (duration) is uncountable: 'I have no time'. 'Times' (occasions) is countable: 'three times'. 'What is the time?' is fine; 'What is the time now by your watch?' is an Indianism.

examples.en: What time is it?
examples.hi: कितने बजे हैं?

examples.en: I don't have time today.
examples.hi: मेरे पास आज समय नहीं है।

examples.en: This is my first time in Delhi.
examples.hi: दिल्ली में यह मेरी पहली बार है।

examples.en: We had a great time at the party.
examples.hi: पार्टी में हमने बहुत अच्छा समय बिताया।

examples.en: I've told you three times already.
examples.hi: मैं आपको पहले ही तीन बार बता चुका हूँ।

common_mistake.wrong: I reached in time for the meeting at exactly ten.
common_mistake.right: I reached on time for the meeting at exactly ten.
common_mistake.why: 'On time' = punctual; 'in time' = early enough, before a deadline.

cloze.sentence: What ____ does the film start?

en_def: a period of twelve months
hi_nuance: Starts with a /j/ sound like 'yes'. 'A year', not 'an year' — the sound is a consonant. 'Years' is plural: 'five years', never 'five year'.

examples.en: I moved here two years ago.
examples.hi: मैं दो साल पहले यहाँ आया था।

examples.en: Happy New Year!
examples.hi: नया साल मुबारक हो!

examples.en: She is in her final year at college.
examples.hi: वह कॉलेज के अंतिम वर्ष में है।

examples.en: The company grew a lot this year.
examples.hi: इस साल कंपनी बहुत बढ़ी।

examples.en: We go to Goa every year.
examples.hi: हम हर साल गोवा जाते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I have an year of experience.
common_mistake.right: I have a year of experience.
common_mistake.why: 'Year' begins with a consonant sound /j/, so it takes 'a'.

cloze.sentence: He is thirty ____ old.

en_def: men, women, and children; persons in general
hi_nuance: 'People' is already plural — 'peoples' is only for nations. 'People are', never 'people is'. Use 'people' instead of 'persons' in normal speech.

examples.en: There were many people at the station.
examples.hi: स्टेशन पर बहुत लोग थे।

examples.en: People say the food here is good.
examples.hi: लोग कहते हैं कि यहाँ का खाना अच्छा है।

examples.en: How many people are coming?
examples.hi: कितने लोग आ रहे हैं?

examples.en: Some people don't like cold weather.
examples.hi: कुछ लोगों को ठंडा मौसम पसंद नहीं है।

examples.en: Most people work five days a week.
examples.hi: ज़्यादातर लोग हफ़्ते में पाँच दिन काम करते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: Two peoples are waiting outside.
common_mistake.right: Two people are waiting outside.
common_mistake.why: 'People' is already plural; 'peoples' means different nations.

cloze.sentence: Many ____ use the metro every day.

en_def: a method of doing something; a road or route; a direction
hi_nuance: 'On the way' = while going somewhere; 'in the way' = blocking. 'By the way' introduces a new topic. 'Which way?' = which direction.

examples.en: Is this the way to the station?
examples.hi: क्या यह स्टेशन जाने का रास्ता है?

examples.en: There is a better way to do this.
examples.hi: इसे करने का एक बेहतर तरीका है।

examples.en: I'll buy milk on the way home.
examples.hi: मैं घर जाते समय रास्ते में दूध खरीद लूँगा।

examples.en: Please move; you're in the way.
examples.hi: कृपया हटिए; आप रास्ते में हैं।

examples.en: By the way, did you see my email?
examples.hi: वैसे, क्या आपने मेरा ईमेल देखा?

common_mistake.wrong: I met him in the way to office.
common_mistake.right: I met him on the way to the office.
common_mistake.why: 'On the way' means during the journey; 'in the way' means blocking.

cloze.sentence: Can you show me the ____ to the exit?

en_def: a period of 24 hours; the time when it is light
hi_nuance: 'Today morning' is an Indianism — say 'this morning'. 'The other day' = a few days ago. 'Day after tomorrow' needs 'the': 'the day after tomorrow'.

examples.en: What day is it today?
examples.hi: आज कौन सा दिन है?

examples.en: I work six days a week.
examples.hi: मैं हफ़्ते में छह दिन काम करता हूँ।

examples.en: Have a nice day!
examples.hi: आपका दिन शुभ हो!

examples.en: It rained all day.
examples.hi: पूरे दिन बारिश हुई।

examples.en: I saw him the other day.
examples.hi: मैंने उसे कुछ दिन पहले देखा था।

common_mistake.wrong: I met her today morning.
common_mistake.right: I met her this morning.
common_mistake.why: 'Today morning' is Indian English; natural English is 'this morning'.

cloze.sentence: Which ____ of the week is best for you?

en_def: an adult male human
hi_nuance: Plural is 'men' (/men/), not 'mans'. The vowel /æ/ is between Hindi 'अ' and 'ए' — the same sound as in 'bad'. Avoid 'man' to mean all people in formal writing; use 'people'.

examples.en: A man is waiting for you outside.
