examples.en: Thank you very much.
examples.hi: बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

examples.en: She speaks very fast.
examples.hi: वह बहुत तेज़ बोलती है।

examples.en: I am very happy with the result.
examples.hi: मैं नतीजे से बहुत खुश हूँ।

examples.en: The exam was not very difficult.
examples.hi: परीक्षा बहुत कठिन नहीं थी।

common_mistake.wrong: I like this film very much good.
common_mistake.right: I like this film very much.
common_mistake.why: 'Very much' modifies the verb; don't add another adjective after it.

cloze.sentence: The soup is ____ hot; be careful.

en_def: truly; very (used for emphasis)
hi_nuance: 'Really?' as a question shows surprise. 'Really' can go before strong adjectives where 'very' cannot: 'really excellent'. Spelling: two 'l's.

examples.en: I really like this song.
examples.hi: मुझे यह गाना सचमुच बहुत पसंद है।

examples.en: Really? I didn't know that.
examples.hi: सच में? मुझे यह पता नहीं था।

examples.en: It was a really good film.
examples.hi: यह वाकई एक अच्छी फ़िल्म थी।

examples.en: Do you really want to leave?
examples.hi: क्या आप सच में जाना चाहते हैं?

examples.en: I'm really sorry for the delay.
examples.hi: देरी के लिए मुझे सचमुच खेद है।

common_mistake.wrong: It was a very excellent presentation.
common_mistake.right: It was a really excellent presentation.
common_mistake.why: 'Very' does not go with extreme adjectives; use 'really' or 'absolutely'.

cloze.sentence: Is it ____ that late already?

en_def: in addition; too
hi_nuance: Position: before the main verb ('I also speak Gujarati'), after 'be'. 'Too' goes at the end ('I speak Gujarati too'). Indian English overuses 'also' at the end: 'I am coming also' → 'I am coming too'.

examples.en: She speaks Hindi and also Marathi.
examples.hi: वह हिन्दी और मराठी भी बोलती है।

examples.en: I also work on weekends sometimes.
examples.hi: मैं कभी-कभी सप्ताहांत में भी काम करता हूँ।

examples.en: The hotel is cheap and also very clean.
examples.hi: होटल सस्ता है और बहुत साफ़ भी है।

examples.en: He is also a good singer.
examples.hi: वह एक अच्छा गायक भी है।

examples.en: We also need to check the logs.
examples.hi: हमें लॉग भी जाँचने होंगे।

common_mistake.wrong: I am coming to the party also.
common_mistake.right: I am coming to the party too.
common_mistake.why: At the end of a sentence, English uses 'too' or 'as well', not 'also'.

cloze.sentence: She is a teacher and ____ a writer.

en_def: no more than; just; single
hi_nuance: Put 'only' next to the word it limits: 'I only have ten rupees' vs 'Only I have ten rupees' mean different things. Indian English adds 'only' for emphasis ('I am from Surat only') — drop it.

examples.en: I have only ten minutes.
examples.hi: मेरे पास सिर्फ़ दस मिनट हैं।

examples.en: She is the only girl in the class.
examples.hi: वह कक्षा में एकमात्र लड़की है।

examples.en: It costs only fifty rupees.
examples.hi: इसकी कीमत सिर्फ़ पचास रुपये है।

examples.en: Only members can enter.
examples.hi: केवल सदस्य ही प्रवेश कर सकते हैं।

examples.en: I was only joking.
examples.hi: मैं सिर्फ़ मज़ाक कर रहा था।

common_mistake.wrong: I am staying in Surat only.
common_mistake.right: I live in Surat.
common_mistake.why: 'Only' for emphasis at the end is Indian English and changes the meaning.

cloze.sentence: There is ____ one seat left.

en_def: a very short time ago; only; exactly
hi_nuance: 'I have just eaten' = a moment ago (present perfect in British English). 'Just' = only: 'just a minute'. Vowel /ʌ/ as in 'cup', begins with /dʒ/.

examples.en: I have just finished lunch.
examples.hi: मैंने अभी-अभी लंच ख़त्म किया है।

examples.en: Just a minute, please.
examples.hi: बस एक मिनट, कृपया।

examples.en: It's just what I wanted.
examples.hi: यह बिल्कुल वही है जो मैं चाहता था।

examples.en: She just left.
examples.hi: वह अभी-अभी गई है।

examples.en: I'm just looking, thanks.
examples.hi: मैं बस देख रहा हूँ, धन्यवाद।

common_mistake.wrong: He came just now before five minutes.
common_mistake.right: He came five minutes ago.
common_mistake.why: Use 'ago' after a period; 'just now' and 'before' together is Hindi-influenced.

cloze.sentence: The train has ____ arrived.

en_def: at the present time
hi_nuance: Diphthong /aʊ/ as in 'cow'. 'Right now' = immediately. 'Now' at the start of a sentence can introduce a new topic. 'From now on' = starting today.

examples.en: I am busy now.
examples.hi: मैं अभी व्यस्त हूँ।

examples.en: What should we do now?
examples.hi: अब हमें क्या करना चाहिए?

examples.en: She lives in Canada now.
examples.hi: वह अब कनाडा में रहती है।

examples.en: From now on, lock your screen.
examples.hi: अब से, अपनी स्क्रीन लॉक करो।

examples.en: Call me now; it's urgent.
examples.hi: मुझे अभी फ़ोन करो; यह ज़रूरी है।

common_mistake.wrong: Now a days, everyone has a phone.
common_mistake.right: Nowadays, everyone has a phone.
common_mistake.why: 'Nowadays' is one word.

cloze.sentence: The shop is closed ____; come back tomorrow.

en_def: at that time; after that; in that case
hi_nuance: Voiced /ð/ — not 'den'. Don't confuse with 'than' (comparison): 'bigger than', but 'first this, then that'. 'Then' at the end = in that case: 'See you at six, then'.

examples.en: First boil the water, then add the tea.
examples.hi: पहले पानी उबालो, फिर चाय डालो।

examples.en: I was a student then.
examples.hi: तब मैं छात्र था।

examples.en: If you're tired, then rest.
examples.hi: अगर आप थके हैं, तो आराम करो।

examples.en: See you at six, then.
examples.hi: तो छह बजे मिलते हैं।

examples.en: We had lunch and then went home.
examples.hi: हमने लंच किया और फिर घर चले गए।

common_mistake.wrong: Delhi is bigger then Jaipur.
common_mistake.right: Delhi is bigger than Jaipur.
common_mistake.why: 'Than' is for comparisons; 'then' is for time or sequence.

cloze.sentence: Finish your homework, and ____ you can play.

en_def: in or to this place
hi_nuance: Same sound as 'hear'. 'Come here' — no 'to'. 'Here you are' / 'Here you go' when handing something over. 'Here is/are' introduces things.

examples.en: Bring the ladder over here.
examples.hi: सीढ़ी यहाँ ले आओ।

examples.en: I have lived here for five years.
examples.hi: मैं यहाँ पाँच साल से रह रहा हूँ।

examples.en: Here is your change.
examples.hi: यह रहे आपके बाकी पैसे।

examples.en: Is there a bank near here?
examples.hi: क्या यहाँ पास में कोई बैंक है?

examples.en: Sign here, please.
examples.hi: कृपया यहाँ हस्ताक्षर करें।

common_mistake.wrong: Please come to here.
common_mistake.right: Please come here.
common_mistake.why: 'Here' takes no preposition after verbs of movement.

cloze.sentence: Wait ____ until I come back.

en_def: in or to that place; used to say something exists (there is / there are)
hi_nuance: Voiced /ð/. 'There is' + singular, 'there are' + plural. Hindi 'है' at the end of a sentence often becomes 'there is' at the start: 'There is a problem'. Don't confuse with 'their' (possessive) or 'they're'.

examples.en: Put the bag over there.
examples.hi: बैग वहाँ रख दो।

examples.en: There is a bug in the code.
examples.hi: कोड में एक बग है।

examples.en: There are many shops on this street.
examples.hi: इस गली में बहुत सी दुकानें हैं।

examples.en: Have you been there before?
examples.hi: क्या आप पहले वहाँ गए हैं?

examples.en: There isn't any milk left.
examples.hi: दूध बिल्कुल नहीं बचा है।

common_mistake.wrong: There is many people in the hall.
common_mistake.right: There are many people in the hall.
common_mistake.why: 'People' is plural, so use 'there are'.

cloze.sentence: ____ are three meetings today.

en_def: on this day
hi_nuance: Stress the second syllable: to-DAY. 'Today morning/evening' is an Indianism — say 'this morning', 'this evening', 'tonight'. Don't say 'on today'.

examples.en: What are you doing today?
examples.hi: आज आप क्या कर रहे हैं?

examples.en: It's very cold today.
examples.hi: आज बहुत ठंड है।

examples.en: I have a meeting today at three.
examples.hi: आज तीन बजे मेरी मीटिंग है।

examples.en: Today is my birthday.
examples.hi: आज मेरा जन्मदिन है।

examples.en: The report is due today.
examples.hi: रिपोर्ट आज देनी है।

common_mistake.wrong: I will call you today evening.
common_mistake.right: I will call you this evening.
common_mistake.why: 'Today evening' is Indian English; use 'this evening'.

cloze.sentence: Is the office open ____?

en_def: on the day after today
hi_nuance: Hindi 'कल' means both yesterday and tomorrow — English separates them. Stress the second syllable. 'The day after tomorrow' = परसों. No 'on' before 'tomorrow'.

examples.en: See you tomorrow.
examples.hi: कल मिलते हैं।

examples.en: Tomorrow is a holiday.
examples.hi: कल छुट्टी है।

examples.en: I have an exam tomorrow morning.
examples.hi: कल सुबह मेरी परीक्षा है।

examples.en: Let's finish this by tomorrow.
examples.hi: चलो इसे कल तक ख़त्म करते हैं।

examples.en: She is leaving the day after tomorrow.
examples.hi: वह परसों जा रही है।

common_mistake.wrong: I will submit it on tomorrow.
common_mistake.right: I will submit it tomorrow.
common_mistake.why: 'Tomorrow' takes no preposition.

cloze.sentence: What are your plans for ____?

en_def: on the day before today
hi_nuance: Always with the past simple: 'I went yesterday', never 'I have gone yesterday'. 'Yesterday night' is wrong — say 'last night'. Stress the first syllable.

examples.en: I met him yesterday.
examples.hi: मैं कल उससे मिला था।

examples.en: Yesterday was very hot.
examples.hi: कल बहुत गर्मी थी।

examples.en: She sent the email yesterday afternoon.
examples.hi: उसने कल दोपहर ईमेल भेजा था।

examples.en: Did you watch the match yesterday?
examples.hi: क्या आपने कल मैच देखा था?

examples.en: The day before yesterday, we went to Surat.
examples.hi: परसों हम सूरत गए थे।

common_mistake.wrong: I have called him yesterday.
common_mistake.right: I called him yesterday.
common_mistake.why: 'Yesterday' is a finished time, so the past simple is required.

cloze.sentence: Where were you ____ evening?

en_def: the early part of the day, from sunrise until noon
hi_nuance: 'In the morning', not 'at morning'. 'This morning', 'tomorrow morning', 'yesterday morning' — no preposition. 'Good morning' as a greeting is fine until noon.

examples.en: I exercise in the morning.
examples.hi: मैं सुबह व्यायाम करता हूँ।

examples.en: Good morning! How are you?
examples.hi: सुप्रभात! आप कैसे हैं?

examples.en: I have a meeting tomorrow morning.
examples.hi: कल सुबह मेरी मीटिंग है।

examples.en: She called this morning.
examples.hi: उसने आज सुबह फ़ोन किया।

examples.en: The morning train is always crowded.
examples.hi: सुबह की ट्रेन हमेशा भीड़ वाली होती है।

common_mistake.wrong: I go for a walk at morning.
common_mistake.right: I go for a walk in the morning.
common_mistake.why: 'Morning' takes 'in the', not 'at'.

cloze.sentence: What time do you wake up in the ____?

en_def: the part of the day between afternoon and night
hi_nuance: Two syllables: EEV-ning. 'In the evening', 'this evening', 'tomorrow evening'. 'Good evening' is a greeting; 'Good night' is only for leaving. 'Tonight' replaces 'today night'.

examples.en: We usually eat dinner at eight in the evening.
examples.hi: हम आमतौर पर शाम आठ बजे रात का खाना खाते हैं।

examples.en: Good evening, everyone.
examples.hi: सबको शुभ संध्या।

examples.en: Are you free this evening?
examples.hi: क्या आप आज शाम खाली हैं?

examples.en: The evenings are cool in October.
examples.hi: अक्टूबर में शामें ठंडी होती हैं।

examples.en: I'll finish it by tomorrow evening.
examples.hi: मैं इसे कल शाम तक ख़त्म कर दूँगा।

common_mistake.wrong: Let's meet today evening.
common_mistake.right: Let's meet this evening.
common_mistake.why: 'Today evening' is Indian English; say 'this evening'.

cloze.sentence: We go for a walk every ____.

en_def: things that people and animals eat
hi_nuance: Uncountable: 'some food', 'a lot of food' — 'foods' only for different types. Long /uː/. Say 'have lunch/dinner', not 'take food'. 'Meal' is one occasion of eating.

examples.en: Indian food is very tasty.
examples.hi: भारतीय खाना बहुत स्वादिष्ट होता है।

examples.en: We need to buy some food.
examples.hi: हमें कुछ खाना खरीदना है।

examples.en: What is your favourite food?
examples.hi: आपका पसंदीदा खाना क्या है?

examples.en: The food at the wedding was excellent.
examples.hi: शादी में खाना बहुत बढ़िया था।

examples.en: Don't waste food.
examples.hi: खाना बर्बाद मत करो।

common_mistake.wrong: Did you take your food?
common_mistake.right: Have you eaten?
common_mistake.why: 'Take food' is Indian English; say 'eat' or 'have a meal'.

cloze.sentence: The ____ here is cheap and good.

en_def: a person whose job is to treat sick people
hi_nuance: 'See a doctor' or 'go to the doctor' — not 'show to the doctor' or 'consult with'. 'Doctor' is used as a title: 'Doctor Sharma'. Stress the first syllable.

examples.en: You should see a doctor.
examples.hi: आपको डॉक्टर को दिखाना चाहिए।

examples.en: My sister is a doctor.
examples.hi: मेरी बहन डॉक्टर है।

examples.en: The doctor gave me some medicine.
examples.hi: डॉक्टर ने मुझे कुछ दवा दी।

examples.en: I have a doctor's appointment at four.
examples.hi: चार बजे डॉक्टर से मेरी अपॉइंटमेंट है।

examples.en: Call a doctor; she is not well.
examples.hi: डॉक्टर को बुलाओ; वह ठीक नहीं है।

common_mistake.wrong: I went to show the doctor.
common_mistake.right: I went to see the doctor.
common_mistake.why: In English you 'see' a doctor; 'show the doctor' is a translation of Hindi 'दिखाना'.

cloze.sentence: The ____ said I need more rest.

en_def: a room or building where people work at desks
hi_nuance: 'Go to the office' — Indian English drops 'the' ('going to office'). 'At the office' = at work. 'Office hours' = working hours. 'In office' (no article) = holding a political position.

examples.en: I'll be at the office until six.
examples.hi: मैं छह बजे तक दफ़्तर में रहूँगा।

examples.en: Our office is on the third floor.
examples.hi: हमारा दफ़्तर तीसरी मंज़िल पर है।

examples.en: She works in a small office.
examples.hi: वह एक छोटे दफ़्तर में काम करती है।

examples.en: The office is closed on Sundays.
examples.hi: दफ़्तर रविवार को बंद रहता है।

examples.en: Please come to my office at ten.
examples.hi: कृपया दस बजे मेरे दफ़्तर आइए।

common_mistake.wrong: I am going to office now.
common_mistake.right: I am going to the office now.
common_mistake.why: 'Office' needs the article 'the'.

cloze.sentence: Is the ____ open on Saturday?

en_def: a device used to talk to people far away; (verb) to call
hi_nuance: 'On the phone' = talking. 'Phone' is more natural than 'mobile' alone in international English. 'Phone number' — not 'contact number' in casual speech. Starts with /f/, diphthong /əʊ/.

examples.en: My phone battery is dead.
examples.hi: मेरे फ़ोन की बैटरी ख़त्म हो गई है।

examples.en: She is on the phone right now.
examples.hi: वह अभी फ़ोन पर है।

examples.en: I'll phone you later.
examples.hi: मैं बाद में आपको फ़ोन करूँगा।

examples.en: Could I borrow your phone for a second?
examples.hi: क्या मैं एक सेकंड के लिए आपका फ़ोन ले सकता हूँ?

examples.en: Turn off your phone during the exam.
examples.hi: परीक्षा के दौरान अपना फ़ोन बंद रखो।

common_mistake.wrong: My mobile is not working. Give me a miss call.
common_mistake.right: My phone is not working. Give me a missed call.
common_mistake.why: Say 'phone', and the adjective is 'missed', not 'miss'.

cloze.sentence: I left my ____ in the car.

en_def: the amount of money you pay for something
hi_nuance: 'Price' is the amount; 'cost' is what you spend. Prices are 'high/low', not 'expensive/cheap' (things are expensive). 'What's the price?' = 'How much is it?'. Ends in /s/, not /z/.

examples.en: What is the price of this shirt?
examples.hi: इस शर्ट की कीमत क्या है?

examples.en: Prices have gone up this year.
examples.hi: इस साल कीमतें बढ़ गई हैं।

examples.en: The price includes delivery.
examples.hi: कीमत में डिलीवरी शामिल है।

examples.en: They sell good phones at a low price.
examples.hi: वे कम कीमत पर अच्छे फ़ोन बेचते हैं।

examples.en: Can you give me a better price?
examples.hi: क्या आप मुझे बेहतर दाम दे सकते हैं?

common_mistake.wrong: The price of this laptop is very expensive.
common_mistake.right: This laptop is very expensive.
common_mistake.why: Prices are 'high' or 'low'; only things can be 'expensive'.

cloze.sentence: The ____ of petrol went up again.

en_def: feeling pleased and satisfied
hi_nuance: 'Happy with' a result, 'happy for' a person, 'happy to' + verb. Vowel /æ/ as in 'bad'. Comparative 'happier', superlative 'happiest'. 'Happy birthday', not 'happy birthday to you' in writing.

examples.en: I am very happy today.
examples.hi: मैं आज बहुत खुश हूँ।

examples.en: She is happy with her new job.
examples.hi: वह अपनी नई नौकरी से खुश है।

examples.en: Happy birthday!
examples.hi: जन्मदिन मुबारक हो!

examples.en: I'm happy to help.
examples.hi: मुझे मदद करके खुशी होगी।

examples.en: They look happy together.
examples.hi: वे साथ में खुश दिखते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I am happy from your work.
common_mistake.right: I am happy with your work.
common_mistake.why: 'Happy' takes 'with' for things and results.

cloze.sentence: Are you ____ with the results?
